items.title: Tee Ball: The First Practice
items.objective: Every child leaves knowing the coaches' names, where the bases are, how to get into a ready position, and that baseball is fun. Nobody stands in a line longer than it takes to say 'your turn'.

blocks.title: Name Circle and Freeze Tag
blocks.description: Gather everyone in a circle on the outfield grass behind first base, coaches included. Go around once: each child says their name and does one jumping jack while everyone repeats the name back. Then play freeze tag inside the cone square; when the coach yells 'Freeze!', everyone stops in a ready position with knees bent and hands on knees like a frog about to jump.
blocks.setup: Four cones in a 30-by-30-foot square on the grass. No balls or bats inside the square. Gloves stay in a pile by the fence until Station A.
blocks.groups: Whole team together, with every parent helper inside the square playing too.
coachingPoints: Learn and use every child's name in the first ten minutes; it is the fastest way to earn their attention.
Call 'Freeze!' five or six times so the ready position becomes a game instead of a lecture.
Keep every instruction to one sentence and show it with your body.

blocks.title: Station A: Alligator Scoops
blocks.description: A parent helper rolls a soft ball slowly to a child from about ten feet away. The child waits in the ready position, then scoops the ball with the glove flat on the grass and the bare hand coming down on top like an alligator chomping. The child runs the ball back to the helper's bucket and the next roll comes right away, so nobody waits.
blocks.setup: Two cones ten feet apart for each pair, one helper with a bucket of six soft balls for every two children. Use grass, not dirt, for the first week so there are no bad hops.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four. Within the group two children field while two run balls back to the bucket, switching every roll. All three stations rotate on the head coach's whistle every 8 minutes.
coachingPoints: Say 'Alligator chomp!' as the ball arrives so both hands come together on it.
Roll slowly and straight at the glove; success comes first and challenge comes later.
Glove fingers point down to the grass for anything below the knees.

blocks.title: Station B: Tee Swings
blocks.description: One child at a time puts on a helmet, steps into the bat zone, and hits soft balls off the tee toward the outfield. The other three stand at the waiting cone, each holding a ball and practicing the knocking-knuckles grip on a spare bat handle laid on the ground, then sprint out to collect the hit balls when the helper calls 'Go!'. Each child takes three swings, sets the bat down inside the zone, and the next child comes in.
blocks.setup: A tee on a throw-down home plate facing the outfield, with a half-circle of four cones ten feet behind and beside it marking the bat zone. One more cone twenty feet away marks the waiting spot. Four soft balls, two helmets, one bat for the hitter.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 8 minutes per rotation. Each child gets two turns of three swings.
coachingPoints: Nobody enters the bat zone until the hitter has laid the bat on the ground.
Point the front shoulder at the field, look at the ball on the tee, and swing level through it.
Praise contact loudly, even a dribbler; this station is about confidence.

blocks.title: Station C: Base Race
blocks.description: The helper walks the group around the bases once, touching each base and saying its name out loud together. Then children run the bases one at a time while the helper jogs alongside calling out the base names. The next runner leaves as soon as the one ahead touches first, so there is always someone moving. Finish with everyone running from third to home together.
blocks.setup: Throw-down bases at your league's tee ball distance, with a bright cone sitting on each base so it cannot be missed. Place one extra cone fifteen feet past first base as the run-through finish line.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 8 minutes per rotation; a new runner starts every time the runner ahead touches first.
coachingPoints: Run through first base, not to it; the cone past the bag is the finish line.
Touch every base with either foot; stepping over the base is the most common mistake.
Turn left after first when running all the way around, and show it rather than explain it.

blocks.title: Game: Everybody Scores
blocks.description: Half the team spreads out on the infield grass in ready positions while the other half hits off the tee one at a time and runs all the way around the bases on every hit. The fielders chase the ball together and carry it to the bucket on the pitcher's mound; if the ball is in the bucket before the runner touches home, the fielders earn a point, and the runner scores no matter what. Switch sides after everyone has hit once.
blocks.setup: Tee at home plate with the bat zone cones still in place, a bucket on the mound, soft balls only, helmets on all hitters and runners. Fielders start at least twenty feet from the tee.
blocks.groups: Two teams of six or seven. One helper runs the bases beside each batter, one helper manages the bat zone, and the head coach cheers from the mound.
coachingPoints: The bat goes on the ground before the hitter runs; a helper stands ready to collect it.
Every runner scores, so celebrate every run with the same enthusiasm.
Fielders carry the ball to the bucket together, which gets every child moving to the ball.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up Circle
blocks.description: Back to the circle on the grass. Ask each child one thing they liked, then show the ready position one more time all together. Tell parents the home assignment and the time of the next practice, then finish with a team cheer, hands in the middle.
blocks.setup: Same cone square as the warm-up. Children carry the equipment to the bucket before sitting down.
blocks.groups: Whole team, with parents invited to stand behind the circle to hear the home assignment.
coachingPoints: End on time; tired four-year-olds remember how practice ended.
Give parents one skill to practice at home, and only one.

safety: Soft or foam balls only; no hard baseballs at any station this week.
Helmets on every hitter and every runner, and one bat in use at a time inside a marked bat zone.
Walk the grass for holes, sprinkler heads, and glass before children arrive.
Water break built into every rotation; four-year-olds will not ask for one.
progressions: Next week roll ground balls slightly faster and from fifteen feet instead of ten.
Add a second tee at the hitting station with a second helper so swings per child double.
In the game, ask fielders to throw the ball to the helper at the bucket instead of carrying it.

items.title: Tee Ball: Throwing and Catching Day
items.objective: Every child can point the glove at a target, step with the opposite foot, and throw a soft ball, and can catch a gentle underhand toss with two hands.

blocks.title: Animal Walks and Arm Circles
blocks.description: Children bear-crawl, crab-walk, and frog-jump between two cone lines twenty feet apart while coaches call out the animals. Finish standing in a spread-out grid doing ten slow arm circles forward and ten backward, arms out like airplane wings, then a full-body wiggle shake.
blocks.setup: Two lines of cones twenty feet apart on the grass. One cone per child on one line so everyone has a home spot.
blocks.groups: Whole team at once, each child on their own cone; nobody waits for a turn.
coachingPoints: Big, slow arm circles; speed is not the point.
Keep it silly and loud so shy children join in.

blocks.title: Team Demo: Point, Step, Throw
blocks.description: Everyone stands on their own cone facing the fence, each holding a soft ball. The coach shows the three parts: point the glove at the target, step toward it with the foot opposite the throwing hand, then throw. The team shadows each part on the coach's words, then on 'Throw!' everyone throws into the fence at once and jogs to collect their own ball.
blocks.setup: Cone grid from the warm-up turned to face a fence or backstop fifteen feet away. One soft ball per child, gloves on.
blocks.groups: Whole team spread on the grid, all throwing on the same command so nobody is behind anyone.
coachingPoints: Say the words with them: 'Point. Step. Throw.'
Check the stepping foot; a right-handed thrower steps with the left foot.
Fingers on top of the ball, thumb underneath, not a palm ball.

blocks.title: Station A: Knock Down the Cones
blocks.description: Children throw soft balls at a row of cones set along the base of the fence from a throw-down 'step spot' about ten to twelve feet away. A helper hands out balls so the thrower never bends to a bucket, and the children run forward to reset the cones they knocked over before stepping back for the next throw. Every knockdown gets a cheer.
blocks.setup: Six cones in a row against the fence, two step spots (throw-down bases or chalk squares) ten to twelve feet back, a bucket of ten soft balls, one helper.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, two children throwing at a time while two reset cones, switching every two throws. Rotate stations every 8 minutes on the whistle.
coachingPoints: Step onto the step spot with the front foot every single throw.
Point the glove at the cone first, then throw.
Aim is the goal here, not how hard the ball goes.

blocks.title: Station B: Two-Hand Catch
blocks.description: Start without gloves: each child tosses a soft ball up a foot and catches it with two hands, thumbs together. Then a helper kneels six feet away and underhand-tosses to the chest, the child catches with thumbs together above the waist or pinkies together below, and rolls it back. Put gloves on for the last three minutes and repeat the same tosses.
blocks.setup: Four cones in a row ten feet apart as catching spots, one helper with a bucket of soft balls kneeling in front, gloves set beside each cone.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, every child on a cone and catching on every round; the helper tosses down the line and back.
coachingPoints: Watch the ball into your hands; the eyes catch it first.
Thumbs together up high, pinkies together down low.
Give the glove a target out front, elbow bent, not stiff.

blocks.title: Station C: Roll, Scoop, Throw
blocks.description: A helper rolls a soft ball to a child ten feet away. The child scoops with the alligator chomp, stands up, points the glove at the helper, steps, and throws back to the helper's glove. If the throw misses, the helper simply picks it up and rolls the next one so the pace never stops.
blocks.setup: Two helpers if you have them, each with a bucket of six soft balls, facing two children each ten feet away with cones marking the spots. Grass only.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, two children per helper; every child fields and throws on every rep.
coachingPoints: Alligator chomp, then stand tall, then point, step, throw.
Throw to the helper's glove, not just in the helper's direction.
Slow rolls that get fielded beat fast rolls that get past.

blocks.title: Game: Clean Your Room
blocks.description: Two teams stand on opposite sides of a cone line twenty feet apart, each with ten soft balls scattered on their side. On 'Go!' both teams throw the balls onto the other side for one minute using point, step, throw; underhand is fine for anyone who wants it. When the coach calls 'Stop!' everyone freezes and counts the balls on their side; fewer balls wins the round. Play three rounds with a water break between each.
blocks.setup: A line of cones across the middle of the grass with a second line twenty feet away on each side as the back boundary. Twenty soft balls, ten per side. No gloves needed.
blocks.groups: Two teams of six or seven, with a helper on each side keeping children behind their cone line.
coachingPoints: Soft balls and one-minute rounds only, three rounds total; this is a throwing game, not a throwing marathon.
Point and step on every throw even in the excitement.
Nobody crosses the middle line; helpers guard it.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up: Show Me Your Throw
blocks.description: Everyone back to their warm-up cone. On the coach's words, the whole team shadows one perfect point, step, throw with no ball, then takes a bow. Tell parents the home assignment is ten minutes of soft-ball catch from six feet.
blocks.setup: Cone grid from the warm-up. Balls collected in the bucket by the children first.
blocks.groups: Whole team on their cones, parents listening from the fence.
coachingPoints: One sentence of praise per child by name if time allows.
Remind parents: short, soft, and fun at home, with the glove target out front.

safety: Soft or foam balls for every throw today; no hard baseballs for this age group.
Everyone throws in the same direction at every station, toward a fence or a helper, never toward another station.
Keep total throws modest: short distances, rest between rounds, and stop any child who says their arm hurts.
No gloves at the face-level catching stage; underhand tosses to the chest only.
progressions: Move the cone targets to fifteen feet and add a bucket target worth two points.
Catching station: helper tosses from eight feet and adds a slow bounce catch.
Replace Clean Your Room with partner catch at eight feet for pairs who are ready.

items.title: Tee Ball: Hitting Stations
items.objective: Every child can set up a stance in the cone boxes, hold the bat with knocking knuckles, and hit a soft ball off the tee while every other child is moving, not watching.

blocks.title: Stance Statues
blocks.description: Children jog between two cone lines; when the coach yells 'Statue!' they freeze in a batting stance with no bat: feet wider than shoulders, knees bent, hands up by the back shoulder as if holding a bat. The coach walks through and gently adjusts feet and hands, then calls 'Go!' for the next jog. Repeat six to eight times with skips and side shuffles mixed in.
blocks.setup: Two lines of cones twenty-five feet apart on the grass; no equipment out yet except the cones.
blocks.groups: Whole team at once, spread along the cone line so everyone has space to freeze.
coachingPoints: Nose over the toes, knees soft, eyes on the imaginary pitcher.
Hands up and back, not down by the belt.
Make the adjustments quick and kind; it is a game.

blocks.title: Station A: Tee Into the Net
blocks.description: One hitter at a time, helmet on, steps into the bat zone and hits five soft balls off the tee into the net from six feet away. The helper resets the ball and checks the knocking-knuckles grip before each swing. The other three children stand at the waiting cone and on each swing do a 'stance statue' with no bat, then rotate in after five swings so everyone hits twice.
blocks.setup: Tee six feet in front of a hitting net or backstop, bat zone marked by a half-circle of cones ten feet around the tee, waiting cone twenty feet to the side and behind. Two helmets, one bat, bucket of soft balls.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, rotating every 9 minutes on the whistle; each child gets two turns of five swings.
coachingPoints: Line up the middle knuckles of both hands on the handle; call them the knocking knuckles.
Set the tee at belly-button height and the ball even with the front hip.
Swing and set the bat down inside the zone before leaving it.

blocks.title: Station B: Grip and Shadow Swings
blocks.description: Each child stands in their own stance box made of two cones, ten feet from the next child, holding a foam bat or a pool noodle, or nothing at all. The helper calls 'Grip!' and checks the knocking knuckles, 'Stance!' and checks the feet, then 'Swing!' and everyone swings slowly at an imaginary ball on an imaginary tee. For the last three minutes each child tries to tap a soft ball balanced on a tall cone in front of their box.
blocks.setup: Four stance boxes made of two cones each, ten feet apart in a row, all facing the same direction toward open grass. Foam bats or pool noodles only, one tall cone with a soft ball balanced on top in front of each box.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, each child in their own box the whole time; nobody waits.
coachingPoints: Knocking knuckles lined up, then hands up by the back shoulder.
Slow swing, hold the finish, eyes stay on the cone.
All swings on the helper's word so nobody swings while a neighbor resets.

blocks.title: Station C: Hit and Hustle
blocks.description: A second tee sits on a throw-down home plate with a single base forty feet away. One child hits a soft ball off the tee, sets the bat down, and runs through the base past the finish cone while the other three, spread out on the grass in ready positions, chase the ball down and bring it to the helper's bucket. Everyone rotates one spot after each hit, so each child hits several times and fields several times.
blocks.setup: Tee on a throw-down plate with a bat zone of cones, one base forty feet away with a finish cone fifteen feet beyond it, bucket of soft balls, two helmets, three fielding cones spread on the grass twenty-five feet from the tee.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four: one hitter, three fielders, rotating after every hit.
coachingPoints: Bat down inside the zone, then run hard through the base.
Fielders start on their cone in a ready position, not next to the hitter.
Run to the finish cone, not to the base.

blocks.title: Game: Everybody Hits, Everybody Runs
blocks.description: Half the team fields with gloves on the infield, half hits off the tee at home plate and runs the bases. Each hitter runs to first on the first hit, then on the next hitter's hit runs on to second, and so on until they score, exactly like a real game but with no outs. Fielders throw or carry the ball to the helper at the pitcher's mound to end the play. Switch sides after everyone has batted once.
blocks.setup: Tee at home plate inside the bat zone cones, bases out with cones on top, a helper on the mound with a bucket, soft balls, helmets for every hitter and runner.
blocks.groups: Two teams of six or seven, one helper coaching the bases, one running the bat zone, the head coach on the mound.
coachingPoints: One hitter in the zone, next hitter waiting at the on-deck cone with no bat.
Runners go when the ball is hit, not before; base helper says 'Go!'.
Cheer the fielders for getting the ball to the mound quickly.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up: Best Swing
blocks.description: Everyone back to the stance boxes with no bats. On the count of three, the whole team takes one slow perfect shadow swing and freezes on the finish while the coaches applaud. Tell parents the home assignment and collect equipment with the children carrying everything to the bucket.
blocks.setup: Cone boxes from Station B. Bats and helmets already collected.
blocks.groups: Whole team in the boxes, parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Name one specific thing each child did well today if time allows.
Remind parents: tee at belly-button height, soft balls, and five swings at a time at home.

safety: One real bat in use at a time, only inside a cone-marked bat zone, and only with a helmet on.
Foam bats or pool noodles at the shadow station, spaced ten feet apart and swinging on command.
Soft balls at every station and in the game; nothing hard is hit today.
The bat is laid down, never thrown; a helper stands at the zone to make sure.
progressions: Move the tee ball to inside and outside positions for children who hit the middle one consistently.
Add gentle soft toss from the side for children who have made contact on every tee swing for two weeks.
In the game, let fielders try a throw to the helper at first base instead of bringing the ball to the mound.

items.title: Coach Pitch: Fundamentals Circuit
items.objective: Players move through a complete circuit of throwing, hitting a moving ball, ground balls, and pop-ups, with one hitting station run under strict helmet and bat-zone rules.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Players spread along the foul line and move to a cone line twenty yards away and back: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, side shuffles facing both ways, and a walking lunge. Finish with arm circles small to big in both directions and ten trunk twists.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the left-field foul line and a matching line twenty yards into the outfield.
blocks.groups: Whole team at once in one wave, a coach leading from the front and a helper at the back.
coachingPoints: Everyone starts and finishes together; it is a team warm-up, not a race.
Arm circles are slow and controlled; the arm is not warmed up yet.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners face each other across the foul line and build the throw in four stages: wrist flips from fifteen feet with the elbow resting in the glove, one-knee throws from twenty feet focusing on the arm circle, standing point-step-throw from thirty feet, then forty feet with a glove target. Each stage lasts about two minutes, and every partner gives a chest-high glove target on every throw.
blocks.setup: Partners in two lines facing each other, fifteen feet apart to start, moving back on the coach's call. Soft baseballs for anyone still nervous, regular balls for the rest. All throws travel the same direction across the line.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by comfort level, with an odd player paired with a helper. Coaches walk behind one line watching the stepping foot.
coachingPoints: Point the glove, step with the opposite foot, and finish with the throwing hand near the opposite knee.
Elbow at shoulder height at the top of the arm circle.
Hit the glove; nobody tries to throw hard today.

blocks.title: Station 1: Hitting Zone
blocks.description: A coach front-tosses soft baseballs from behind an L-screen or a bucket twelve to fifteen feet in front of the hitter, who hits into the backstop or a net. The hitter takes six swings and rotates. One player waits at the on-deck cone twenty feet away doing slow dry swings, and the other two feed balls to the coach's bucket from behind the screen, so all four are busy.
blocks.setup: Bat zone marked by cones in a fifteen-by-fifteen-foot square around home plate; only the hitter and the tossing coach are inside it. On-deck cone twenty feet up the first-base line, L-screen or bucket in front of the coach, two helmets, soft baseballs.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 10 minutes on the head coach's whistle. Inside the group, rotate after every six swings: hitter to feeder, feeder to on-deck, on-deck to hitter.
coachingPoints: Helmets on both the hitter and the on-deck player before anyone picks up a bat.
Bat-zone rule: nobody crosses the cones while a hitter holds a bat, and the bat is set down inside the zone when the turn ends.
Watch the ball from the coach's hand all the way to the bat.
Short, level swing; if the ball goes up in the air a lot, the hands are dropping.

blocks.title: Station 2: Ground Ball Triangle
blocks.description: A helper rolls firm ground balls from twenty feet to a player set up in the fielding triangle: feet wider than the shoulders, glove out front on the ground, bare hand above it. The player fields, funnels the ball to the belly, steps, and throws to a second helper standing on a base cone twenty feet away. Two players field alternately while two back up the throws at the base and swap every four balls.
blocks.setup: Two fielding spots marked with cones on the infield dirt or grass, a helper with a bucket of regular baseballs twenty feet in front, a base cone twenty feet to the side with a second helper receiving throws.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation; two fielders and two backups swapping every four ground balls.
coachingPoints: Feet wide, glove out in front of the toes, so the player can see the ball into the glove.
Funnel the ball to the belly, then point, step, and throw.
Move the feet to get in front of the ball before it arrives.

blocks.title: Station 3: Pop-Ups
blocks.description: A helper tosses soft balls underhand fifteen to twenty feet into the air to players spread out in the outfield grass. The player moves the feet to get under the ball, calls 'Ball, ball, ball!' three times, and catches with two hands above the eyes, thumbs together. Two players catch alternately while two retrieve any drops and toss them back to the helper's bucket.
blocks.setup: Four cones in a square twenty feet on a side in shallow outfield grass, one helper in the middle with a bucket of soft balls. Soft balls only until every player is catching confidently.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation, every player catching every other toss.
coachingPoints: Call it three times, loud, before the ball comes down.
Get under the ball with the feet first; the glove goes up last.
Thumbs together above the eyes, and use two hands.

blocks.title: Game: Hit and Run the Bases
blocks.description: Half the team takes the field and half bats. The coach pitches from a short distance, each batter gets three pitches to put the ball in play or runs anyway on the third, and the defense tries to get the ball to first base. Offense scores a run for every batter who reaches first; defense earns a point for every clean field-and-throw to first, whether or not the runner is out. Switch sides after everyone bats once.
blocks.setup: Full infield with bases, a coach pitching from about twenty feet with soft baseballs, helmets for all batters, bat zone cones still around home plate, a helper at first base.
blocks.groups: Two teams of six or seven, a helper coaching first base and another managing the batting order and bat zone.
coachingPoints: Reward the clean play, not just the out; the score is about execution.
Run through first base every time.
Fielders set up in the ready position before every pitch.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Team takes a knee along the foul line. Ask three questions: what do we point at before we throw, what do we say three times under a pop-up, and where does the bat go when your turn is over. Announce the home assignment and finish with a cheer.
blocks.setup: Foul line, equipment already collected into the buckets by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team, parents listening behind them.
coachingPoints: Let players answer the questions, not coaches.
Hand out exactly one home assignment.

safety: Helmets on the hitter and the on-deck player at all times; one bat in the hitting zone at a time.
Bat-zone rule posted on a cone: nobody enters the cone square while a bat is being swung, and the bat is set down inside the zone before the hitter leaves.
Soft baseballs for all front toss and pop-ups; regular baseballs only on rolled ground balls and partner catch.
Throwing progression builds from short to long; stop any player who reports arm pain and tell a parent.
progressions: Front toss from eighteen feet with a slightly firmer toss for hitters making consistent contact.
Ground balls thrown with a hop instead of rolled, and the throw goes to a player at first base instead of a helper.
Pop-ups tossed to the side so players practice moving right and left before catching.

items.title: Coach Pitch: Ground Ball Day
items.objective: Every player fields a rolled ground ball in the triangle, uses the correct glove angle for low and high balls, and makes a throw to first base, while one group at a time hits in a helmet-and-bat-zone station.

blocks.title: Ready Position Freeze
blocks.description: Players jog, skip, and shuffle between two cone lines; on 'Ready!' everyone drops into a ready position: feet wider than shoulders, knees bent, hands out in front, weight on the balls of the feet. The coach walks the line tapping shoulders of players who are set correctly, and the next movement starts on 'Go!'.
blocks.setup: Two lines of cones twenty-five feet apart on the outfield grass.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, spaced an arm's length apart.
coachingPoints: Hands out front, not on the knees, for this age group.
Weight forward so a little hop happens naturally.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty, standing throws at thirty, then forty feet with a glove target. Finish with ten quick-catch throws at twenty-five feet where the goal is to catch and release smoothly, which previews the transfer station.
blocks.setup: Partners facing each other across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, all throwing the same direction.
blocks.groups: Pairs, odd player with a helper; coaches walk behind one line.
coachingPoints: Step toward the partner's glove on every throw.
Quick catch means smooth, not rushed; the ball stays in the glove until the feet are set.

blocks.title: Station 1: Rolled Ground Balls in the Triangle
blocks.description: A helper rolls regular baseballs on the grass from twenty feet to a player set in the fielding triangle. The player fields with the glove on the ground out in front of the toes and the bare hand on top, funnels to the belly, and tosses underhand back to the helper. Two field alternately while two shag anything that gets by and refill the bucket, swapping every five balls.
blocks.setup: Two fielding cones twenty feet in front of a helper with a bucket of twelve baseballs. Grass, with the dirt saved for next week.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, rotating every 10 minutes on the whistle; two fielders and two shaggers switching every five balls.
coachingPoints: Glove on the ground before the ball gets there, not swiping at it.
Feet wider than shoulders, nose over the ball.
Funnel to the belly every time, even on an easy one.

blocks.title: Station 2: Glove Angles, Fingers Down and Fingers Up
blocks.description: A helper stands eight feet away and tosses soft balls underhand, alternating between knee-high and chest-high. Below the waist the player turns the glove fingers down; above the waist the glove turns fingers up. Players call out 'Down!' or 'Up!' before the catch. In the last three minutes the helper mixes in a short bounce so the player learns to stay low on a hopping ball.
blocks.setup: Four cones in a row ten feet apart, players on the cones, a helper walking the line with a bucket of soft balls.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, every player on a cone and catching every round.
coachingPoints: Fingers down below the belt, fingers up above it.
Two hands on every catch; the bare hand covers the ball.
Stay low on bounces; do not stand up to a low ball.

blocks.title: Station 3: Hitting Zone
blocks.description: Hitters alternate between the tee and gentle front toss from a coach behind a bucket twelve feet away, hitting soft baseballs into the net or backstop. Six swings each, then rotate. The on-deck player does dry swings at the on-deck cone twenty feet away; two feeders keep the coach's bucket full from behind the coach.
blocks.setup: Cone square fifteen feet on a side around home plate marking the bat zone, tee and net inside, on-deck cone up the first-base line, two helmets, soft baseballs.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 10 minutes; inside the group rotate hitter, feeder, feeder, on-deck after every six swings.
coachingPoints: Helmets on for the hitter and the on-deck player, and nobody else touches a bat.
Bat-zone rule: the cones are a wall while a bat is in a hitter's hands.
Hit the top half of the ball so it goes on the ground; today is ground ball day for the fielders too.

blocks.title: Team: Field It, Throw It to First
blocks.description: Players take infield positions with a helper at first base. The coach rolls or hits easy fungo ground balls to one position at a time, the fielder uses the triangle, funnels, steps, and throws to first. After each ball every player moves one position clockwise so everyone fields from several spots.
blocks.setup: Infield with bases, coach at home plate with a bucket, a helper receiving at first base, two players at each infield position when numbers allow.
blocks.groups: Whole team on the infield, rotating one position after each ball; outfielders rotate in at third base.
coachingPoints: Everyone in the ready position before the coach touches the ball.
Throw to the helper's chest; a good throw matters more than a fast one.
Move your feet, then field; do not reach.

blocks.title: Game: Beat the Record
blocks.description: Same setup as the team segment. The coach rolls or hits ground balls one after another, and the team counts out loud every clean play: fielded cleanly and thrown so the first-base helper can catch it without leaving the base. A bobble or a bad throw does not reset the count; it just does not add to it. The team tries to beat its own record from the previous practice.
blocks.setup: Infield positions, a helper at first, a bucket of twenty baseballs at home plate.
blocks.groups: Whole team, rotating one position after every ball so every player gets several plays.
coachingPoints: The team record belongs to everyone, so cheer every clean play by name.
Keep the pace quick; the next ball comes as soon as the fielder is reset.
Execution counts, not speed: a slow clean play scores, a rushed bad throw does not.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee on the infield grass. Ask the team to show the fielding triangle with no ball and to call out 'Down!' and 'Up!' as the coach holds a glove low and high. Announce the record, the home assignment, and finish with a cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass, balls collected by the players into the bucket.
blocks.groups: Whole team, parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Write the clean-play record somewhere you will remember for next week.
One home assignment, and remind parents to roll on grass.

safety: Rolled ground balls on grass for Station 1; nothing is hit hard at a seven-year-old.
Helmets on the hitter and the on-deck player, one bat in the zone, and the bat set down inside the zone when a turn ends.
Soft balls at the glove-angle station and in the hitting zone.
Everyone throws toward first base in the team segment; no cross-field throws.
progressions: Move Station 1 to the infield dirt and roll from thirty feet.
Add a backhand roll to the glove-angle station for players who are turning the glove correctly.
In Beat the Record, require the first-base helper to catch the throw with one foot on the base.

items.title: Coach Pitch: Baserunning and Games
items.objective: Players run through first base, round first on a ball to the outfield, know when they are forced to run, and finish with a small-sided game that scores good decisions as highly as runs.

blocks.title: Run-Through Warm-Up
blocks.description: Dynamic movements from the foul line to a cone line twenty yards out: jog, skips, high knees, side shuffles, arm circles. Then players line up two at a time at home plate and sprint through first base to a cone fifteen feet past the bag, slowing down only after the cone. A helper at first says 'Through!' as they pass.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line, a matching line twenty yards out, bases in place, a bright cone fifteen feet past first base in foul territory.
blocks.groups: Whole team for the dynamic part, then pairs sprinting side by side on the coach's 'Go!' so the wait is never more than one pair.
coachingPoints: Run through the base and past the cone; the cone is the finish line, not the bag.
Hit the front half of the base with either foot; no leaping at it.
Eyes up after the base; look for an overthrow, but that is a later lesson.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty, standing point-step-throw at thirty, then forty feet to a glove target. Keep it to about two minutes per stage and remind everyone the arm is a tool for the whole season.
blocks.setup: Partners in two facing lines, all throws traveling the same direction across the foul line, soft baseballs for nervous catchers.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by comfort, odd player with a helper, coaches walking behind one line.
coachingPoints: Step toward the glove on every throw.
Catch with two hands and bring the ball to the chest before throwing back.

blocks.title: Station 1: Hitting Zone, Hit and Go
blocks.description: A coach front-tosses soft baseballs from behind an L-screen or bucket twelve to fifteen feet away. Each hitter takes five swings, and on the fifth swing sets the bat down inside the zone and sprints to a cone forty feet up the first-base line as if running out a hit. The on-deck player waits at the on-deck cone doing dry swings, and the other two feed balls from behind the screen.
blocks.setup: Bat zone marked by a cone square around home plate, L-screen or bucket in front of the coach, on-deck cone twenty feet up the first-base line and a sprint cone forty feet out, two helmets, soft baseballs. Use a plate in foul territory if the infield is needed for Station 2.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 10 minutes on the whistle; inside the group rotate hitter, feeder, feeder, on-deck after each hitter's sprint.
coachingPoints: Helmets on the hitter and the on-deck player; nobody else holds a bat.
Bat-zone rule: the cones are a wall while a bat is in anyone's hands, and the bat goes on the ground before the sprint.
Hit it, drop it, go: the habit of running on contact starts here.

blocks.title: Station 2: The Banana Turn
blocks.description: Players learn to round first on a ball hit to the outfield. A cone sits eight to ten feet outside the baseline about two-thirds of the way to first; the runner bends out around the cone, touches the inside corner of the base with either foot, and takes a few hard steps toward second before stopping. Two players run at a time on the helper's 'Hit!' while the other two wait at the on-deck cone, then swap.
blocks.setup: Use a spare base in the outfield so the infield stays free: a throw-down home plate, a base sixty feet away, a banana cone eight to ten feet outside the straight path, and a stop cone fifteen feet past the base toward the imaginary second base.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation, two runners going at a time from side-by-side plates.
coachingPoints: Bend out early, not at the last second; the path looks like a banana.
Touch the inside corner and lean toward second.
Look at where the ball is while rounding; the helper points to it.

blocks.title: Station 3: Force or Tag?
blocks.description: A helper acts as pitcher with a soft ball, with one runner on a throw-down first base, one fielder at second, one fielder at first, and one batter-runner at home with no bat. On 'Hit!' the helper rolls to a fielder; because the batter-runner is coming to first, the runner on first is forced and the fielder only has to touch second. Then the helper removes the batter-runner, rolls again, and the group has to notice the runner is not forced and must be tagged. Rotate every two plays.
blocks.setup: Throw-down bases forty feet apart in the outfield grass forming home, first, and second; one helper with soft balls as the pitcher; a cone where the batter-runner starts.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, rotating roles every two plays: runner, batter-runner, fielder at first, fielder at second.
coachingPoints: Ask before every roll: 'Is the runner forced?' and make the whole group answer.
A force play means touch the base; a tag play means touch the runner with the ball in the glove.
Tag softly with the back of the glove; nobody swipes at a face.

blocks.title: Game: Hit and Run Scrimmage
blocks.description: Half the team fields, half bats, coach pitching soft baseballs from a short distance with a maximum of three pitches per batter. Offense scores one run for every runner who scores and one bonus point for every good baserunning decision the base coach calls out: running through first, taking the banana turn on a ball to the outfield, or stopping when a line drive is caught. Defense scores a point for every clean field-and-throw to the correct base, out or not. Switch sides after everyone bats once.
blocks.setup: Full infield with bases, coach pitching from about twenty feet, helmets on every batter and runner, bat-zone cones around home plate, helpers coaching first and third base.
blocks.groups: Two teams of six or seven, with helpers as base coaches and the head coach pitching and keeping score out loud.
coachingPoints: Announce every bonus point by name so good decisions get as much noise as runs.
Runners look at the base coach before every pitch; the coach uses a windmill for go and two hands up for stop.
Fielders in the ready position before every pitch, and the ball goes to the base the play is at.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee on the infield grass. Ask the team two questions: when do we run through first base, and when does a fielder have to tag the runner. Announce the home assignment and finish with the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected into the buckets by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players answer, coaches confirm.
Tell parents the home assignment is a baserunning lesson that needs no equipment at all.

safety: Helmets on every batter, on-deck player, and runner; one bat in the hitting zone at a time, set down inside the zone before running.
Soft baseballs for all front toss and for the Force or Tag station.
Tags are made with the glove below the shoulders; no diving tags and no collisions, and runners slow down before an occupied base in practice.
Baserunning stations use spare bases in the outfield so no one runs through a live throwing lane.
progressions: Add a base coach at Station 2 who decides whether the runner holds or keeps going to second.
In Force or Tag, add a second runner on second base so players sort out two forces at once.
Let a player pitch underhand from close range in the scrimmage once the group handles coach pitch well, if your division allows it.

items.title: Minors: Infield Fundamentals
items.objective: Every infielder fields a fungo ground ball in the triangle, handles a short hop and a backhand with the right glove angle, and uses right-left-throw footwork to make an accurate throw to first.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: From the foul line to a cone line twenty-five yards out and back: jog, high knees, butt kicks, carioca both directions, side shuffles in a ready position, and walking lunges with a trunk twist. Finish with arm circles small to large and ten slow trunk rotations.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the left-field line and a matching line twenty-five yards into the outfield.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave with a player captain leading from the front.
coachingPoints: Side shuffles stay low, like fielding a ground ball on the move.
Nobody throws until the whole warm-up is done.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners build the throw in five stages of about two minutes each: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five feet with a full arm circle, the rocker step at forty feet (step back with the throwing-side foot, then forward into the throw), regular throws at sixty feet, then back in to forty-five feet for quick-catch, which means catching and releasing in rhythm with the feet moving. Today ends at sixty feet; this is not long toss.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, all throws in the same direction. Regular baseballs.
blocks.groups: Pairs by arm comfort, odd player with a coach, one coach walking behind each line watching the front shoulder and stepping foot.
coachingPoints: Front shoulder points at the target before the arm goes.
Elbow at shoulder height at the top; finish with the throwing hand near the opposite knee.
Quick-catch is smooth, not hurried: catch, turn, step, throw in one rhythm.

blocks.title: Station 1: Fungo Triangle and Funnel
blocks.description: A coach hits easy fungo ground balls from forty to fifty feet to one fielder at a time on the infield dirt between second and third. The fielder sets up in the triangle, fields the ball out in front, funnels it to the belly, and throws to a player standing on the first-base bag. Two fielders alternate while one receives at first and one backs up the throw, swapping roles every five balls.
blocks.setup: Coach with a fungo bat and a bucket of baseballs near the mound, two fielding cones on the dirt between second and third, a player receiving at first base, a backup player ten feet behind first in foul territory.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 10 minutes on the whistle: two fielders, one receiver, one backup, swapping every five ground balls.
coachingPoints: Approach under control and get the feet set before the ball arrives.
Glove out in front where the eyes can see the ball into it; funnel to the belly.
Throw to the chest of the receiver; the receiver gives a two-hand target.

blocks.title: Station 2: Short Hops and Backhand Intro
blocks.description: Partners stand fifteen feet apart on the grass with tennis balls. One throws a firm one-hopper that bounces three or four feet in front of the fielder, who stays low and catches the short hop with the glove moving forward, not back. After three minutes the thrower aims to the fielder's throwing-arm side so the fielder turns the glove over for a backhand: glove-side foot forward, glove fingers pointing down, eyes on the ball into the glove. Switch roles every six balls.
blocks.setup: Pairs of cones fifteen feet apart on grass, one tennis ball per pair, gloves on. Tennis balls keep bad hops painless while the glove angles are being learned.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation, working in pairs the whole time so everyone fields constantly.
coachingPoints: Play the hop you want: go get the short hop instead of waiting for the in-between hop.
Backhand with the glove-side foot forward and fingers down; watch it in.
Stay low from start to finish; standing up is the most common mistake.

blocks.title: Station 3: Right-Left-Throw to the Net
blocks.description: A helper rolls a ground ball from twenty-five feet to a fielder who fields it, then says the footwork out loud: 'Right, left, throw' for a right-handed thrower (left, right, throw for a lefty), shuffling toward the target with each step and throwing into a net with a taped strike zone thirty-five feet away. Two fielders alternate while two collect balls from behind the net and refill the bucket.
blocks.setup: A hitting net with a taped or chalked square about the size of a player's chest, thirty-five feet from a fielding cone, a helper with a bucket of baseballs twenty-five feet in front of the fielder.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation, two fielding alternately and two retrieving, swapping every five balls.
coachingPoints: Say the footwork out loud until the feet do it without thinking.
The shuffle steps carry the fielder toward the target so the throw is shorter and straighter.
Hit the square, not the net; accuracy is the whole point of the footwork.

blocks.title: Team: Infield at Positions
blocks.description: Players take all infield positions, with extra players doubling up behind the regulars and outfielders rotating in. The coach hits fungo to one spot at a time and the fielder throws to first, but every other infielder has a job too: on a ball to the left side the second baseman covers second, on a ball to the right side the shortstop covers second, and the pitcher backs up or covers first on a ball to the first baseman. After each ball the coach asks one player where they went and why.
blocks.setup: Full infield with bases, coach at home plate with a fungo bat and a bucket, a catcher in gear or a helper receiving return throws, extra players standing ten feet behind each position.
blocks.groups: Whole team on the infield, the doubled-up players swapping in after every two ground balls.
coachingPoints: Everybody moves on every ball; nobody watches.
Know who covers second before the ball is hit, and say it out loud.
Throws to first are chest-high; a good throw beats a hard one.

blocks.title: Game: 21 Outs
blocks.description: Same positions as the team segment. The coach hits ground balls in rapid order and the team counts out loud every clean play: fielded cleanly and thrown chest-high to first so the first baseman never leaves the bag. A bobble or a bad throw takes the count back two, but never below the last multiple of seven reached, so a hot streak is protected. The team wins when it reaches twenty-one clean plays, or sets a record to beat next week.
blocks.setup: Full infield, coach with a fungo bat and a full bucket at home, a player at first base and a backup in foul territory behind first.
blocks.groups: Whole team at positions, rotating one spot clockwise every three ground balls so everyone fields from several places.
coachingPoints: Celebrate the seven, fourteen, and twenty-one marks loudly as a team.
A slow, clean play counts; a fast, wild one does not.
Keep the pace: the next ball is hit as soon as the fielder is set.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Ask the team to show the triangle and say the footwork out loud together. Announce the 21 Outs result, the home assignment, and finish with a cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass, balls collected by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team, parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Name two players who did something well that nobody else noticed.
Remind players the home assignment can be done with a tennis ball against a wall.

safety: Fungo ground balls are hit at a pace the fielder can handle; fielders who are not confident get rolled balls from the coach first.
Tennis balls at the short-hop station until every player keeps the glove out front on bad hops.
All throws in a station go to a single target; receivers wear a glove and give a target, and nobody stands behind the receiver except in foul territory.
Throwing progression ends at sixty feet; players who pitched in the last game throw only the first three stages and tell the coach how the arm feels.
progressions: Hit fungo from home plate at game distance once the triangle is automatic from forty feet.
Replace tennis balls with baseballs at the short-hop station for players who are consistently out front.
Add a runner with a helmet to 21 Outs so the throw has to beat someone.

items.title: Minors: Hitting Stations
items.objective: Every hitter takes quality swings at three tee locations, against front toss, and in a bat-control drill, then applies them in coach-pitch batting practice with a live defense, all inside helmet and bat-zone rules.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line twenty-five yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, carioca, side shuffles, walking lunges with a trunk twist. Finish with arm circles and ten slow hip rotations each direction, since the hips do the work in a good swing.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a matching line twenty-five yards into the outfield.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, a player captain leading.
coachingPoints: Hip rotations are slow and balanced on both feet.
Finish together before anyone picks up a ball.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then quick-catch at forty-five. Two minutes per stage, glove targets every throw, and the coaches watch for the front shoulder pointing at the target.
blocks.setup: Partners in two facing lines, all throws the same direction, regular baseballs.
blocks.groups: Pairs by arm comfort, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Point the front shoulder, step, and finish across the body.
Nobody tries to throw hard; this is preparation, not a contest.

blocks.title: Station 1: Tee Locations
blocks.description: Three cones on the ground mark where the tee goes for an inside pitch (even with the front foot, closer to the plate), a middle pitch (off the front hip), and an outside pitch (deeper, toward the back foot, on the outer edge). The hitter takes four swings at each location into the net, with the helper moving the tee and calling the location. The on-deck player does slow shadow swings at the on-deck cone, and two players collect balls behind the net and reset the bucket.
blocks.setup: Hitting net eight feet in front of a throw-down plate, tee, three location cones, a bat zone of cones around the plate, on-deck cone twenty feet away, two helmets, a bucket of baseballs.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 11 minutes on the whistle; inside the group, rotate after each hitter's twelve swings.
coachingPoints: Inside pitch: hit it out front and pull it. Outside pitch: let it get deeper and hit it the other way.
Same stance and same load for every location; only the contact point changes.
Helmets on the hitter and the on-deck player, one bat in the zone, bat on the ground before leaving.

blocks.title: Station 2: Front Toss Behind the L-Screen
blocks.description: A coach kneels behind an L-screen fifteen feet in front of a plate set ten feet from the backstop and tosses firm underhand pitches that the hitter drives into the backstop. Eight swings per turn, with the first two taken at half speed to find the timing. The on-deck player shadows the load and stride at the on-deck cone, and two feeders keep the coach's bucket full from behind the screen.
blocks.setup: Throw-down plate ten feet in front of the backstop, L-screen fifteen feet in front of the plate, bat zone cones, on-deck cone twenty feet away in foul territory, bucket of baseballs, two helmets.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 11 minutes per rotation; rotate hitter, feeder, feeder, on-deck after every eight swings.
coachingPoints: Small load: a slight shift of the weight back as the coach's arm goes back, so the swing starts on time.
Hands take a short path to the ball; the barrel stays above the hands until contact.
The coach stays behind the screen on every toss, no exceptions.

blocks.title: Station 3: Bat Control, Top Hand and Bottom Hand
blocks.description: At the outfield fence a helper kneels at a forty-five-degree angle in front of the hitter and soft-tosses tennis balls. The hitter chokes up to the middle of the bat and takes five swings with the top hand only, five with the bottom hand only, then five with both hands, hitting each ball into the fence. The other three players each stand in their own cone box fifteen feet apart doing the same one-hand shadow swings with no ball so the whole group is working.
blocks.setup: A plate twelve feet from the outfield fence, a kneeling helper with a bucket of tennis balls forty-five degrees in front of the hitter on the open side, a bat zone of cones, three shadow-swing cone boxes fifteen feet apart and well outside the zone, two helmets.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 11 minutes per rotation; one hitter at the fence while three shadow-swing, rotating after fifteen swings.
coachingPoints: Top-hand swings: elbow stays close to the body, palm up at contact.
Bottom-hand swings: pull the knob to the ball, no casting out.
Shadow swingers hold the finish for two seconds, balanced.

blocks.title: Team: Coach-Pitch Batting Practice With Defense
blocks.description: The coach pitches overhand from behind an L-screen at a shortened distance while the rest of the team plays defense at real positions. Each hitter takes five swings and runs out the fifth, and the defense plays every ball live, including throwing to first. Two hitters wait in the on-deck area behind the backstop fence, and everyone rotates from the outfield to the infield to the on-deck area to the plate.
blocks.setup: Full field with bases, L-screen in front of the mound, a full bucket for the coach, a catcher in gear or a helper behind the plate, helmets for hitters and on-deck players, bat zone cones.
blocks.groups: Whole team: one hitter, two on deck behind the fence, everyone else on defense, rotating one spot after each hitter.
coachingPoints: Same swing from the stations: small load, short path, finish balanced.
Defense plays every ball as if a runner were going, because one is on the fifth swing.
On-deck players stay behind the fence until the hitter has set the bat down.

blocks.title: Game: Hard-Contact Points
blocks.description: Two teams alternate hitters against the coach's front toss from the L-screen. A line drive scores three, a hard ground ball scores two, any other fair ball scores one, and a swing and miss scores nothing but gets another toss. The result on the field does not matter, only the quality of contact, and the defense calls out the points honestly. First team to twenty-five wins, or the higher total when time runs out.
blocks.setup: Same field setup as the team segment, two team lists on a clipboard, one hitter at a time with helmets on the hitter and the next two.
blocks.groups: Two teams of five to seven, alternating hitters, three swings each, while the non-hitting players field.
coachingPoints: Hard contact is the only goal; a line drive caught at shortstop still scores three.
Keep the game moving: three tosses, next hitter.
Defense scores it honestly and loudly.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Ask hitters where the tee goes for an inside pitch and an outside pitch, and ask them to show the small load with no bat. Announce the home assignment and finish with a cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected into buckets.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players describe the three tee locations in their own words.
Remind parents the home assignment needs only a tee and a net or fence.

safety: Helmets on every hitter and on-deck player; one bat per bat zone, set down inside the zone when the turn ends.
The coach tosses only from behind an L-screen in both front-toss blocks; tennis balls for the soft-toss station with the helper kneeling at forty-five degrees, never in front.
On-deck players stand behind a fence or at a cone at least twenty feet from any hitter.
Shadow-swing boxes are fifteen feet apart and swings happen on the helper's command.
progressions: Add a fourth tee location, high and low, so hitters adjust bat path as well as contact point.
Front toss with mixed speeds so hitters have to hold the load a little longer.
Batting practice with a player pitching within a strict counted number of pitches, once you have checked the league's pitch-count rules.

items.title: Minors: Outfield and Cutoffs
items.objective: Every player drop-steps to a fly ball, fields an outfield ground ball two ways, and throws to a cutoff man who is lined up and loud, then the whole team runs a cutoff and relay play from start to finish.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up With Drop Steps
blocks.description: Standard dynamic movements from the foul line to a cone line twenty-five yards out and back, then footwork: players face the coach in a spread grid and on 'Left!' or 'Right!' drop-step that way (open the hip and step back with that foot) and sprint three steps, then jog back. Finish with arm circles and arm swings across the body.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line, a matching line twenty-five yards out, and a grid of one cone per player in the outfield facing the coach.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, then everyone on their own cone for the drop-step calls.
coachingPoints: Drop step with the foot on the side the ball is going, then turn and run.
Eyes stay on the coach's hand, like watching the ball off the bat.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression With the Crow Hop
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, standing throws at forty-five, then crow-hop throws at seventy feet. The crow hop is a hop onto the throwing-side foot, a step with the glove-side foot toward the target, and a throw with the whole body behind it. Finish at fifty feet with easy throws to bring the arm back down.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, all throws in the same direction, regular baseballs.
blocks.groups: Pairs by arm comfort, odd player with a coach walking the line.
coachingPoints: The crow hop gains ground toward the target; it is not a jump straight up.
Throw through the partner's chest, long and low, not high and rainbow-shaped.
Seventy feet is the longest throw today; nobody shows off.

blocks.title: Station 1: Drop Step and Fly Balls
blocks.description: A helper stands fifteen feet in front of a fielder, points left or right, and throws a fly ball over that shoulder so the fielder has to drop-step, turn, run, and catch with two hands above the eyes. Start with thrown fly balls at half effort; move to fungo only if every player is catching cleanly. Two fielders alternate while two return balls to the bucket, switching every four balls.
blocks.setup: Two fielding cones in the outfield grass thirty feet apart, a helper with a bucket of regular baseballs fifteen feet in front of them, open grass behind.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 10 minutes on the whistle: two fielders alternating, two retrieving, swapping every four fly balls.
coachingPoints: Drop step first, then run; do not backpedal.
Catch above the eyes with two hands, the glove-side foot slightly forward, ready to throw.
Call it: 'Ball, ball, ball!' even with nobody near you, so the habit forms.

blocks.title: Station 2: Outfield Ground Balls
blocks.description: A helper rolls or throws ground balls from forty feet to an outfielder who fields two ways. The safe way, with nobody on base: get in front, drop the throwing-side knee to the grass to block the ball, and come up throwing. The do-or-die way, when a run is on the line: field the ball on the glove-side foot while moving forward and crow hop into the throw. Throws go to a player standing on a cone sixty feet away acting as the cutoff man.
blocks.setup: Fielding cone in the outfield, a helper with a bucket forty feet in front, a cutoff cone sixty feet toward the infield with a player on it, a backup player behind the cutoff.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation: fielder, cutoff, backup, retriever, rotating every three ground balls.
coachingPoints: Say which way you are fielding before the ball comes: 'Block!' or 'Do or die!'
Throw to the cutoff man's glove side, chest high, so the cutoff can turn and throw.
The cutoff man gives a big two-hand target and yells the outfielder's name.

blocks.title: Station 3: Cutoff Position and Relay Footwork
blocks.description: Three players stand in a line sixty feet apart in the outfield with a fourth as the retriever. The end player throws to the middle player, who is the relay: hands up over the head, calling 'Hit me!', catching on the glove side, turning toward the glove side, and throwing to the third player in one motion. The ball goes down the line and back, then players rotate so everyone takes the middle spot.
blocks.setup: Three cones in a straight line sixty feet apart along the outfield, one baseball per line, a bucket for extras.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation, rotating positions in the line every six throws.
coachingPoints: Hands up and loud: the thrower needs to see and hear the relay man.
Catch on the glove side and turn that way; turning the wrong way wastes a full second.
Short, firm, accurate throws beat long heroic ones.

blocks.title: Team: Cutoffs and Relays Walkthrough
blocks.description: Full defense takes the field and the coach walks through three plays, first with no ball, then with a fungo, then with a runner in a helmet. Play one: single to right field with a runner on second, where the first baseman lines up between the right fielder and home as the cutoff man and the catcher yells 'Cut!' or 'Let it go!'. Play two: single to left with a runner on second, where the third baseman is the cutoff man. Play three: ball in the left-center gap with a runner on first, where the shortstop runs out as the relay man, the second baseman covers second base, and everyone else backs up a base.
blocks.setup: Full field with bases, coach with a fungo bat and bucket at home, a catcher in gear, one or two runners in helmets, cones placed where each cutoff man should stand for the first run-through.
blocks.groups: Nine on defense with extras as runners and backups, rotating after each play so every player is a cutoff or relay man at least once.
coachingPoints: Line up: the cutoff man stands on a straight line between the outfielder and the base the throw is going to.
The catcher runs the play with his voice; the cutoff man listens, not looks.
Every player not in the play backs up a base; nobody stands and watches.

blocks.title: Game: Relay Race
blocks.description: Two teams form relay lines of four players sixty feet apart from the outfield fence to the infield. On 'Go!' the ball travels down each line and back. Points are for execution, not speed: two points for every throw caught by the relay man without moving his feet more than one step, one point if he had to move, zero for a drop or a throw over his head. First team to fifteen points wins; the team that finishes first gets nothing extra.
blocks.setup: Two parallel lines of four cones each, sixty feet apart, starting at the outfield fence; one ball per team, a coach watching each line to award points.
blocks.groups: Two teams of five to seven, with extras rotating in after each trip down and back.
coachingPoints: Accuracy wins this game, so take the extra half second to set the feet.
Relay men keep their hands up and their voices loud all game.
Call the points out loud so players see that execution is what gets rewarded.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee in shallow center field. Ask who the cutoff man is on a single to right with a runner on second and who runs out for the relay on a ball in the gap. Announce the home assignment and finish with the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Outfield grass, equipment collected into buckets by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players answer, coaches confirm.
Tell parents the home assignment includes a relay game they can play in the yard.

safety: Fly balls are thrown, not hit, until every player in the group is catching with two hands above the eyes.
Longest throw of the day is seventy feet in the progression; players who pitched recently stop at forty-five and tell a coach how the arm feels.
Relay lines are spaced so no throw crosses another line, and retrievers stay out of the throwing lanes.
Runners wear helmets in the walkthrough, and fielders never tag a runner at full speed in practice.
progressions: Fungo fly balls at Station 1 with the fielder starting from a real outfield position.
Add a second runner to the walkthrough so the catcher has to decide which base to send the throw to.
Relay Race with five players per line and a throw to a catcher at home plate to finish.

items.title: Minors: Situational Defense
items.objective: Every player knows where to go on a force play at second, who covers each base and who backs up on common plays, and how the pitcher and catcher handle plays at home and first, then proves it in a game that scores decisions, not outs.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line twenty-five yards out and back: jog, high knees, butt kicks, carioca, side shuffles low in a ready position, walking lunges. Finish with arm circles and trunk twists, then a quick 'point to your position' game where the coach calls a position number and everyone points to it.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a matching line twenty-five yards out.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave with a player captain leading.
coachingPoints: Position numbers: pitcher one, catcher two, first base three, second base four, third base five, shortstop six, left seven, center eight, right nine.
Everyone finishes together before any ball comes out.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression Around the Bases
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty feet. Finish with three minutes of base-to-base throws: four players stand on the bases and throw home to first to second to third to home, with the next four waiting at cones and swapping in every trip around.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line for the first four stages, then bases with a player on each and waiting cones in foul territory.
blocks.groups: Pairs for the progression, then groups of four on the bases, swapping every full trip around the diamond.
coachingPoints: Catch with two hands, turn toward the glove side, step, throw.
Chest-high throws: the receiver should never leave the base.

blocks.title: Station 1: Force Play at Second
blocks.description: A helper rolls ground balls from forty feet to a shortstop or a second baseman, who fields and feeds the player covering second with a firm underhand toss from close range or a short overhand throw from farther out. The player covering catches, touches the base with one foot, and finishes with a step toward first, without throwing. Players rotate among fielder, covering player, and the two retrievers, switching every three balls.
blocks.setup: Second base with a fielding cone on each side (shortstop side and second-base side), a helper with a bucket forty feet in front near the mound, two retriever cones on the outfield grass.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 10 minutes on the whistle, roles changing every three ground balls.
coachingPoints: Show the ball before the underhand feed; no wrist flips, firm and chest high.
The covering player gets to the base early and gives a target with both hands.
Touch the base, then clear it: step toward first so a runner cannot collide with you.

blocks.title: Station 2: Covering Bases and Backing Up
blocks.description: On the first-base half of the infield, four players take pitcher, first base, second base, and right field, and the helper calls a play before rolling a slow ground ball: wide to the first baseman, so the pitcher runs to cover first; a single to right field, so the second baseman covers second and the pitcher backs up the throw; a throw to first from the left side, so the right fielder backs up first base. Walk it first, then jog it, then run it, rotating positions every three plays.
blocks.setup: First base, second base, and the mound, with cones marking where the pitcher should run to cover first and where the right fielder should stand to back up; a helper with a bucket at home plate.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation, rotating positions every three plays so every player covers and backs up.
coachingPoints: The pitcher breaks toward first on every ball hit to the right side, every time.
Backing up means standing thirty feet behind the base in line with the throw, not next to the base.
Say your job out loud as the ball is rolled: 'Covering!' or 'Backing up!'

blocks.title: Station 3: Pitcher and Catcher Plays at Home and First
blocks.description: A catcher in full gear sets up behind the plate with a pitcher on the mound, a first baseman, and a batter-runner with a helmet and no bat. The helper rolls a slow dribbler in front of the plate: the catcher yells 'One!', the pitcher or catcher fields it and throws to first. Then the helper tosses a soft ball off the backstop as a passed ball: the catcher goes to get it while the pitcher sprints in to cover home and gives a low target. Rotate roles every two plays, with every player trying the catcher's job in gear.
blocks.setup: Home plate, the mound, first base, a catcher in full gear, soft balls for the passed-ball toss, baseballs for the dribblers, a helper beside the plate.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 10 minutes per rotation: catcher, pitcher, first baseman, batter-runner, rotating every two plays.
coachingPoints: The catcher calls the play because he sees the whole field.
On a passed ball the pitcher covers home immediately, straddling the plate on the inside edge, not standing on it.
Fielder with the ball takes a breath, sets the feet, and throws chest high.

blocks.title: Team: Situations
blocks.description: Full defense on the field with two or three runners in helmets. Before every fungo the coach announces the situation out loud, for example 'Runner on first, one out,' and the whole defense repeats it. The coach hits the ball, the defense makes the play, and the coach freezes everyone immediately after to ask one player where they went and why. Runners run at half speed and peel off before any tag.
blocks.setup: Full field with bases, coach with a fungo bat and a bucket at home, catcher in gear, extra players as runners with helmets waiting at a cone near the dugout.
blocks.groups: Nine on defense, two or three runners, rotating after every three plays so everyone plays several positions and runs once.
coachingPoints: Repeat the situation out loud before every pitch; it is the habit that wins games.
Where does the ball go, who covers, who backs up: three jobs on every play.
The freeze-and-ask takes ten seconds; do not let it turn into a speech.

blocks.title: Game: Defense vs. Offense
blocks.description: Same field and same runners, but now points are scored when the coach calls the situation and hits the ball. Defense earns two points for throwing to the correct base and one more for completing the play cleanly; offense earns two points for every runner who makes the correct decision, going or holding, whether or not they are safe. Nobody earns points for being fast or for an out that came from a wrong decision. First side to fifteen, then switch.
blocks.setup: Full field, coach at home with fungo and bucket, catcher in gear, runners in helmets, a helper keeping score on a clipboard and announcing it.
blocks.groups: Half the team on defense, half as runners with a batter-runner each play, switching sides at fifteen points or after five minutes.
coachingPoints: Announce why each point was earned so the thinking is public.
A right decision with a bad throw still earns two; a wrong decision with a great throw earns zero.
Runners run under control and avoid every tag in practice.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Quiz three situations: ball to the first baseman, who covers first; passed ball, who covers home; single to right, who covers second. Announce the home assignment and the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players answer, coaches confirm and praise.
Remind parents the home assignment is a reading lesson they can do together on the couch.

safety: Catchers wear full gear at Station 3 and in all team segments; a batter-runner never carries a bat.
Runners wear helmets, run at half speed in the team segment, and peel off before tags; fielders tag the air beside the runner in practice.
Soft balls for the passed-ball toss off the backstop.
Throwing progression ends at sixty feet, and players who pitched in the last game skip the base-to-base throws.
progressions: Add a runner on second to the force-play station so the shortstop has to check the lead runner before feeding.
Run the covering and backing-up station on the third-base side with left field backing up third.
In Situations, let a player call the situation out loud instead of the coach.

items.title: Majors: Pre-Season Evaluation Practice
items.objective: Coaches see every player throw, field, hit, and run in game-like reps and record private notes to plan positions and the season's teaching, while players experience a practice that feels like a normal, encouraging day of baseball rather than a tryout.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line thirty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, carioca both ways, side shuffles, walking lunges with a twist, and two build-up sprints at seventy percent. Finish with arm circles, arm swings across the body, and trunk rotations. A coach explains that today is about seeing everyone's baseball so the season's practices can be planned, and that effort is what gets noticed.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a matching line thirty yards into the outfield; clipboards for the coaches with one line per player.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, led by a coach.
coachingPoints: Set the tone: this is a practice, not a ranking.
Build-up sprints are the first look at running form; do not comment on speed.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression With Observation
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then ninety feet for three minutes, then back to sixty for quick-catch. Coaches walk behind the lines and privately note arm action, accuracy, and footwork for each player, saying nothing about it out loud except a correction or a compliment to the individual.
blocks.setup: Partners in two facing lines across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, regular baseballs, one coach behind each line with a clipboard.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Look for the front shoulder pointing at the target and the elbow at shoulder height.
Note who needs the throwing-faults lesson, quietly; it becomes their home assignment.
Ninety feet is the longest throw today, and anyone who pitched this week stops at sixty.

blocks.title: Station 1: Infield Evaluation
blocks.description: Each player fields six fungo ground balls from the shortstop area and throws to a player at first base: three straight at them, two to the backhand side, and one slow roller they have to charge. The coach notes footwork, hands, and throw accuracy. The other three players rotate as the first baseman, the backup behind first, and the retriever, so everyone fields their six and receives throws.
blocks.setup: Coach with a fungo bat and bucket at home plate, fielding cone at shortstop, player at first base, backup cone in foul territory behind first.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 12 minutes on the whistle; inside the group rotate after each player's six ground balls.
coachingPoints: Feet set, glove out front, funnel, right-left-throw: coach says the same cues to every player.
Slow roller: charge under control, field off the glove-side foot, throw on the run.
Praise the clean play out loud; keep the notes private.

blocks.title: Station 2: Outfield Evaluation
blocks.description: Each player takes four fly balls, two over each shoulder so the drop step shows, and two ground balls with a throw to a cutoff player on a cone at the edge of the infield. Fly balls are thrown by the helper first and hit with a fungo only for players who are clearly comfortable. The coach notes first-step direction, route, and whether the throw reaches the cutoff man chest-high.
blocks.setup: Helper with a bucket in shallow center field, fielding cone in medium center, cutoff cone at the infield edge with a player on it, backup player behind the cutoff.
