blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation: fielder, cutoff, backup, retriever, rotating after each player's six balls.
coachingPoints: Drop step, run, catch above the eyes with two hands.
Ground balls: block with the knee when there is time, do-or-die when the helper yells 'Runner!'
Hit the cutoff man; distance is not the goal.

blocks.title: Station 3: Hitting Evaluation
blocks.description: Each hitter takes five swings off the tee into the net, then eight swings of front toss from a coach behind an L-screen into the backstop. The coach notes stance, load, bat path, and contact quality, not distance. The on-deck player shadows at the on-deck cone, and two feeders work behind the screen, so all four are busy.
blocks.setup: Tee and net beside the backstop, a plate ten feet in front of the backstop with an L-screen fifteen feet out, bat zone cones, on-deck cone twenty feet away, two helmets, bucket of baseballs.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation; rotate hitter, feeder, feeder, on-deck after each hitter's thirteen swings.
coachingPoints: Helmets on the hitter and the on-deck player, one bat in the zone, bat set down before leaving it.
Watch for a balanced finish; a hitter who falls over is swinging too hard for today.
Say one encouraging, specific thing to every hitter.

blocks.title: Team: Baserunning Form and Times
blocks.description: Players run home to first through the bag in pairs, then home to second with a banana turn, while a coach quietly records times on the clipboard. Times are never announced and players are never compared out loud; the coach talks only about form, like running through the bag and bending early into the turn. Each player runs twice to first and once to second with walking recovery between.
blocks.setup: Bases in place, a cone fifteen feet past first base, a banana cone outside the baseline, a coach with a stopwatch and clipboard at first base and another at second.
blocks.groups: Whole team in pairs starting on the coach's 'Go!', the next pair starting as soon as the previous pair clears first.
coachingPoints: Run through first, bend early for second, and touch the inside corner of the bag.
Times stay on the clipboard; form is the only public feedback.
Walk back; the recovery is part of the plan.

blocks.title: Game: Controlled Scrimmage
blocks.description: A coach pitches from behind an L-screen so no player's arm carries a pitching workload at the first practice. Each half inning starts with a situation the coach announces, such as a runner on first with one out, and the hitter gets a maximum of four pitches. Coaches watch for game awareness: knowing the outs, covering and backing up, and base running decisions. Play as many half innings as time allows, rotating positions every inning.
blocks.setup: Full field, L-screen in front of the mound, catcher in full gear, helmets on all hitters and runners, a full bucket for the coach, a helper keeping the rotation list.
blocks.groups: Two teams of five to seven, rotating positions each half inning so coaches see players at several spots.
coachingPoints: Announce the situation and ask the defense to repeat it before the pitch.
Note who knows where to go, not who is biggest or fastest.
Every player gets infield and outfield time today.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Thank the team for the effort, tell them every player will have a defined role and that positions will rotate early in the season, and ask what one thing each player wants to get better at. Announce the home assignment and the team cheer. Coaches compare notes privately afterward.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: No rankings, no position announcements, no comparisons.
Use each player's stated goal in a later practice so they know you listened.

safety: No player pitches at the evaluation practice; the coach pitches from behind an L-screen, and pitching evaluations happen later on a counted plan.
Helmets on every hitter, on-deck player, and runner; one bat per bat zone, set down inside the zone when a turn ends.
Longest throw is ninety feet; anyone who pitched in a game this week stops at sixty and the coach notes it.
Base-running times are recorded privately and never read aloud; evaluation never becomes public comparison.
progressions: Second evaluation practice two weeks later with player-pitched innings on a counted plan that follows the league's pitch-count and rest table.
Add a catcher-specific station for the two or three players who want to try the position.
Use the notes to build each player's first home assignment from the lesson that fits them best.

items.title: Majors: Double Plays and Infield Communication
items.objective: Infielders feed the double play firmly and accurately, pivot at second base with safe footwork, and talk before every pitch, and the whole team turns clean double plays against fungo with no runners before adding them.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line thirty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, carioca, side shuffles in a low ready position, walking lunges, two build-up sprints. Finish with arm circles and quick-feet drills: players chop their feet in place and on 'Right!' or 'Left!' shuffle two steps that way and set.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a matching line thirty yards into the outfield.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave led by a player captain.
coachingPoints: Shuffles stay low with the glove hand out front.
Quick feet, quiet feet: no stomping, just rhythm.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression to Quick-Catch
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then ninety feet for two minutes, then back to forty feet for quick-catch. Quick-catch today has a goal: catch with two hands, transfer the ball to the throwing hand as the feet move, and release in rhythm, exactly what a double-play pivot asks for.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, regular baseballs.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Transfer happens in front of the chest while the feet are already moving.
Smooth is fast; rushing causes drops.
Ninety feet is the longest throw today.

blocks.title: Station 1: Feeds
blocks.description: A helper rolls ground balls from forty feet to a shortstop or a second baseman within fifteen feet of the base. The fielder fields, pulls the glove away to show the ball, and feeds the player at the bag with a firm underhand toss, chest-high, following the toss with a step. From farther away the feed becomes a short overhand throw from the ear with no wind-up. Rotate feeder, receiver, and two retrievers every four balls.
blocks.setup: Second base with a fielding cone fifteen feet to each side, a helper with a bucket near the mound, two retriever cones on the outfield grass.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 12 minutes on the whistle; inside the group, roles change every four feeds.
coachingPoints: Show the ball, then feed; the receiver must see it leave the hand.
Firm and chest-high: a soft lob is the slowest play in baseball.
Follow the feed with the feet so the body stays balanced.

blocks.title: Station 2: Pivots at Second Base
blocks.description: A helper feeds from the shortstop side and from the second-base side while one player at the bag learns one simple pivot for each. From the shortstop side as the second baseman: straddle the bag, catch, drag the right foot across the base, step toward first, and throw. From the second-base side as the shortstop: catch while coming across the bag, touch it with the right foot, and throw in the same motion. The throw goes to a player on the first-base bag, with a backup behind.
blocks.setup: Second base, first base with a receiver and a backup cone in foul territory behind it, a helper with a bucket on the infield grass feeding from both sides.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation: pivot player, first baseman, backup, retriever, rotating every five pivots.
coachingPoints: Get to the bag early and wait for the feed; the ball is faster than the feet.
Pick one footwork and repeat it; the assistant coach teaches the same one.
Clear the bag after the throw so a runner cannot hit you.

blocks.title: Station 3: First Base Footwork and the 3-6-3
blocks.description: The first baseman finds the bag with the back heel, sets up with the glove-side foot ready to stretch, and receives throws from a helper on the infield grass, stretching only after seeing where the throw is going. Then the 3-6-3: the helper rolls a ground ball to the first baseman, who fields it and throws to the shortstop covering second, and the shortstop throws back to a second player covering first. Rotate every four plays.
blocks.setup: First base, second base with a cone where the shortstop covers, a helper with a bucket near the mound, a second player covering first for the return throw.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation: first baseman, shortstop at second, player covering first on the return, retriever.
coachingPoints: Find the bag with the heel, then look for the ball.
On the 3-6-3 the throw to second is to the inside of the bag, away from the runner's path.
Keep throws short and firm; this station is about footwork, not arm strength.

blocks.title: Team: Full Double-Play Rotation
blocks.description: Full infield with a catcher in gear and outfielders backing up bases. Before every fungo the whole infield says the play out loud: 'Two!' when there is a runner on first and fewer than two outs, or 'One!' when there is not. The coach hits to each infielder and the team turns the double play with no runner for the first ten minutes. Add a runner in a helmet from home to first only once feeds and pivots are consistently clean, and never a runner sliding into second this week.
blocks.setup: Full field with bases, coach at home with a fungo bat and bucket, catcher in gear, outfielders at their positions, a runner cone near the dugout with helmets.
blocks.groups: Nine on defense with extras rotating in at every infield spot after three plays; outfielders rotate into the infield during the second ten minutes.
coachingPoints: Say the play before the pitch; the loudest infield is usually the best one.
Feed, pivot, throw: three clean parts beat one fast one.
Outfielders back up second and first on every play.

blocks.title: Game: Turn Two Challenge
blocks.description: With the same defense, the coach hits ground balls one after another and the team counts clean turns out loud. A clean turn is a clean field, a chest-high feed, a pivot with the base touched, and an on-target throw to first, regardless of how fast it happened. A bad throw or a missed base does not count and does not subtract. The team tries to reach ten clean turns in ten minutes or beat its own record.
blocks.setup: Full infield, coach with a fungo bat and a full bucket at home, catcher in gear, a helper counting out loud.
blocks.groups: Whole team at positions, rotating infielders every two plays so every player is part of several turns.
coachingPoints: Execution is the only thing counted; the stopwatch stays in the bag.
Everyone says 'Two!' before each ball.
Celebrate each clean turn by naming all three players involved.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Ask what the infield says before the pitch with a runner on first and fewer than two outs, and ask one player to describe the feed in their own words. Announce the home assignment and the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players answer; coaches confirm.
Remind players the home assignment can be done with a wall and a tennis ball for the transfer.

safety: No live runner slides into second base this week; pivots are learned with no runner, then with a runner going only from home to first.
Runners wear helmets and fielders clear the bag after every pivot.
Longest throw is ninety feet in the progression; feeds and station throws are short and firm, not maximum effort.
Check your league's current rulebook for its sliding rules and interference rules before adding runners at second in a later week.
progressions: Add a runner from first to second who runs to the outside of the bag and does not slide, so pivots happen with someone coming.
Introduce the 5-4-3 double play from third base and the 1-6-3 from the pitcher.
Turn Two Challenge with a stopwatch only after every player's footwork is clean for two weeks.

items.title: Majors: Bunt Defense and Baserunning
items.objective: Every player can lay down a sacrifice bunt, every infielder knows their job on a bunt with runners on, and runners round bases and slide safely, all brought together in a bunt-and-run game.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up With Running Form
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line thirty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, carioca, side shuffles, walking lunges with a twist. Finish with two build-up sprints from home through first base past a cone fifteen feet beyond the bag, running in pairs, then arm circles and arm swings.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a line thirty yards out; bases in place with a run-through cone past first.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, then pairs for the sprints.
coachingPoints: Run through first, not to it.
Build-up sprints are about form; nobody races.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then ninety feet for two minutes, then quick-catch at forty-five. Today's quick-catch adds a charge: the receiver takes two steps forward as the ball arrives, like fielding a bunt and throwing on the move.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, regular baseballs.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Front shoulder at the target, elbow up, finish across the body.
On the charging quick-catch, the throw comes from the ear with a short arm action.

blocks.title: Station 1: Bunting
blocks.description: A coach front-tosses soft baseballs from behind an L-screen twenty feet away. The hitter squares around as the coach's arm comes forward, bat at the top of the strike zone, top hand pinching the bat behind the barrel with the fingers safely behind it, and catches the ball with the bat so it rolls toward one of two cones placed ten feet down the first-base and third-base lines. Six bunts per turn, then rotate. The on-deck player shadows the bunt stance at the on-deck cone and two feeders work behind the screen.
blocks.setup: Plate in foul territory or at home, L-screen twenty feet in front, two target cones down each line, bat zone cones, on-deck cone twenty feet away, two helmets, soft baseballs.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 12 minutes on the whistle; inside the group rotate hitter, feeder, feeder, on-deck after each six bunts.
coachingPoints: Bat at the top of the zone and angled up; anything above the bat is a ball, so let it go.
Catch the ball with the bat; do not push at it.
Fingers behind the barrel, never wrapped around it, and helmets on for the hitter and on-deck player.

blocks.title: Station 2: Bunt Defense Footwork
blocks.description: On the infield with no runners, four players take pitcher, catcher in gear, first base, and third base while the helper rolls bunts from home plate. On every roll the catcher yells the base, 'One!' for first, as the fielder charges, fields the ball with the glove and bare hand together, and throws to the base the catcher called while the helper plays first baseman if needed. Rotate positions every three bunts so everyone fields a bunt and everyone makes the call.
blocks.setup: Home plate, the mound, first and third bases, a helper with a bucket of baseballs rolling from the plate, catcher's gear.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation: pitcher, catcher, first baseman, third baseman, rotating every three plays.
coachingPoints: The catcher calls the base because he sees everything; the fielder listens.
Field the ball with two hands and set the feet toward the target before throwing.
Pitcher and third baseman charge; the first baseman charges only if the pitcher cannot get there and otherwise covers first.

blocks.title: Station 3: Baserunning, Rounding and Sliding
blocks.description: In the outfield grass, a throw-down home plate and first base with a banana cone outside the baseline for rounding practice, two runners at a time. Then sliding: players remove nothing but run in cleats on grass to a towel base and practice the bent-leg slide, one leg tucked under in a figure four, sitting down on the back pocket, hands up. Start with slides from a jog and stay with grass only. Check your league's current rulebook for its sliding rules, including head-first rules, before teaching anything beyond the feet-first slide.
blocks.setup: Throw-down plate and base sixty feet apart in the outfield grass, a banana cone, a stop cone, and a towel laid flat forty feet from a start cone for sliding, on grass checked for sprinkler heads and holes.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation; two runners rounding at a time for six minutes, then sliding one at a time from a jog.
coachingPoints: Bend out early for the banana turn and touch the inside corner.
Slide early, sit down on the back pocket, hands up so they do not catch the ground.
Nobody slides into a real base today, and nobody slides head first.

blocks.title: Team: Full Bunt Defense With Runners
blocks.description: Full defense with a catcher in gear and runners in helmets. Play one: runner on first, bunt rolled by the coach; the pitcher and third baseman charge, the second baseman covers first, the shortstop covers second, the catcher calls the base, and the play goes to first unless the ball is fielded quickly enough to get the lead runner. Play two: runners on first and second; the third baseman holds near the bag and the pitcher takes the bunt toward third, with the shortstop covering third if the third baseman charges. Walk each play with no ball, then with a rolled ball, then with runners running under control.
blocks.setup: Full field with bases, coach at home rolling or softly bunting from a bucket, catcher in gear, runners with helmets waiting at a cone by the dugout.
blocks.groups: Nine on defense, two or three runners, rotating after every three plays so every player takes an infield spot and runs once.
coachingPoints: Say the play before the pitch: 'Runner on first, bunt play, go to one!'
Catcher calls the base; everyone else does their job silently and fast.
Runners never slide in this segment; they run through or peel off.

blocks.title: Game: Bunt-and-Run
blocks.description: Two teams: the offense starts every inning with a runner on first and must bunt on the first strike; the coach front-tosses from the L-screen. Offense earns two points for a bunt that advances the runner and one point for a good read by the runner, going on a ball on the ground and holding on a popped-up bunt. Defense earns two points for throwing to the correct base and one for completing the play cleanly. Three outs or four batters ends the half inning, then switch.
blocks.setup: Full field, L-screen in front of the mound with a coach and soft baseballs, catcher in gear, helmets on all hitters and runners, a helper keeping score aloud.
blocks.groups: Two teams of five to seven switching after each half inning.
coachingPoints: Points are for decisions and execution; a safe runner after a wrong call earns the defense nothing and the offense only its read point.
Runners read the bunt: ground ball go, pop-up freeze.
The catcher still calls every base out loud.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Ask who covers first on a bunt with a runner on first, who calls the base, and where the bat sits in the zone for a bunt. Announce the home assignment and the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players answer; coaches confirm.
Remind players the bunting home assignment uses a sock ball or a tennis ball and a wall.

safety: Bunting uses soft baseballs from behind an L-screen with the top-hand fingers behind the barrel; helmets on the hitter and on-deck player, one bat per zone.

Sliding is taught on grass into a towel from a jog, feet first only; no slides into a real base, and no head-first slides until you have checked your league's current rulebook and taught the technique separately.
Runners in helmets run under control in the team segment and never collide with a fielder at a base.
Catcher in full gear for every segment with a bunt or a play at the plate.
progressions: Bunt for a base hit: drag bunts toward third for right-handers and push bunts past the pitcher, if your lineup can already sacrifice reliably.
Add the first-and-third bunt defense with the catcher deciding whether to go for the lead runner.
Sliding into a loose base on grass from a run, once the bent-leg slide looks safe from a jog for two weeks.

items.title: Majors: Pitcher and Catcher Development
items.objective: Pitchers build a balanced, repeatable delivery and catchers learn to receive and block, every pitch is counted on a card, and the whole team learns pitcher fielding plays, with the coach setting each pitcher's workload before practice from the league's configured pitch-count and rest table.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up and Workload Check
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line thirty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, carioca, side shuffles, walking lunges, two build-up sprints, then arm circles small to large, arm swings across the body, and trunk rotations. While players warm up, the head coach confirms the plan written before practice: which pitchers are eligible to throw today based on the pitches they threw in recent games and the league's rest table, how many pitches each will throw, and who will catch.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a line thirty yards out; the coach's pitch log and a blank count card for each pitcher throwing today on a clipboard.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave led by a player captain while the head coach reviews the clipboard with the parent helper who will keep counts.
coachingPoints: Decide workloads before practice, not on the mound; the league's configured pitch-count and rest table is the authority, and the current rulebook is where you confirm it.
Ask every pitcher how the arm feels today; a player who reports soreness does not pitch and the parent is told.
Pitchers who pitched recently can still do dry delivery work with no ball.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression With the Towel Drill
blocks.description: Everyone does the standard progression: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then back to forty-five for easy throws. Pitchers who are scheduled to throw today finish with the towel drill: holding a small towel instead of a ball, they go through the full delivery and snap the towel at a coach's glove held out in front where the release point should be. Pitchers on a rest day do only the towel drill.
blocks.setup: Partners across the foul line, regular baseballs, a small hand towel for each pitcher, a coach kneeling with a glove out front for the towel drill.
blocks.groups: Pairs for the progression, then pitchers with the pitching coach for the towel drill while everyone else does quick-catch.
coachingPoints: Full arm circle, elbow at shoulder height, finish over the front leg.
The towel drill teaches the release point out front with zero stress on the arm.
Sixty feet is the longest throw today for everyone.

blocks.title: Station 1: Pitcher Delivery Work
blocks.description: Every group visits this station because most eleven- and twelve-year-olds will pitch at some point. Players learn the delivery in parts on flat ground: the balance point with the front knee lifted and held for two seconds, the hand break with thumbs down, the stride straight at the target with the front shoulder closed, and a finish over the bent front leg. Scheduled pitchers throw a set number of flat-ground pitches from forty feet to a partner, every one counted on their card by the helper; everyone else repeats the parts dry and throws nothing from this station.
blocks.setup: Flat grass with a throw-down plate and a line to a target plate forty feet away, two cones marking the stride line, a parent helper with the count cards and a pencil.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 15 minutes on the whistle; inside the group, scheduled pitchers throw their counted flat-ground pitches while the others do dry work beside them.
coachingPoints: Balance point: tall, still, and quiet for two seconds before anything moves toward home.
Stride foot lands on the line toward the target; the front shoulder stays closed until the foot lands.
Every pitch thrown here is written down, including the easy ones; the card is the truth.

blocks.title: Station 2: Catcher Receiving and Blocking
blocks.description: One player at a time wears the full gear and gets in the catcher's stance, first the relaxed primary stance with nobody on base, then the ready secondary stance with the backside up. A helper tosses soft balls from fifteen feet: receive with the glove relaxed and the thumb under, catching the ball and holding it still for a count. Then blocking: the helper tosses soft balls into the dirt in front of the catcher, who drops to both knees, tucks the chin, rounds the shoulders, and keeps the ball in front. Every player tries both in gear so the team finds its catchers.
blocks.setup: A throw-down plate on the dirt in front of the backstop, full catcher's gear in one or two sizes, a helper with a bucket of soft balls fifteen feet in front, a cone where the waiting players stand off to the side.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 15 minutes per rotation, each player getting three to four minutes in the gear while the others practice the stance and the blocking motion without gear from the side.
coachingPoints: Relaxed glove, thumb under, catch it and hold it still.
Block with the body, not the glove: knees down, chin tucked, glove fills the hole between the knees.
Soft balls only for blocking until the technique is automatic.

blocks.title: Station 3: Pitcher Fielding Practice
blocks.description: On the first-base side of the infield, one player pitches a dry delivery from the mound, a helper rolls a ground ball to the first baseman, and the pitcher breaks toward first, runs a path toward the inside of the baseline, takes a flip from the first baseman, and touches the inside of the bag. Next: a comebacker rolled to the pitcher, who fields, checks an imaginary runner, and throws to first. Last: a soft ball tossed off the backstop as a passed ball, so the pitcher sprints to cover home while the catcher retrieves. Rotate every two plays.
blocks.setup: The mound, first base, home plate, a helper with baseballs and soft balls near the plate, a cone marking the pitcher's path to first, catcher's gear for whoever covers the passed-ball play.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 15 minutes per rotation: pitcher, first baseman, catcher, retriever, rotating every two plays.
coachingPoints: The pitcher breaks to first on every ball hit to the right side, before knowing if he is needed.
Run to the inside of the bag and touch it with the right foot, then turn in toward the infield.
On a passed ball the pitcher covers home with a low target and gives the catcher a clear throwing lane.

blocks.title: Team: Counted Bullpen
blocks.description: Two or three scheduled pitchers throw a short bullpen to catchers in full gear while the parent helper holds the count card and calls the count out loud every five pitches. The number each pitcher throws was set before practice from the league's configured pitch-count and rest table and the pitches they threw in recent games; the bullpen stops at that number even if the last pitch was a bad one. Everyone else runs pitcher fielding practice and baserunning on the other side of the field with a coach.
blocks.setup: Bullpen mound or a flat-ground plate at pitching distance for your division, catcher in full gear, a parent helper with the count card, a net behind the catcher if there is no backstop; the rest of the team on the far half of the field.
blocks.groups: Pitchers and catchers with the pitching coach and the helper; everyone else with the second coach doing covering-first and baserunning work.
coachingPoints: Count every pitch, including warm-up pitches, and stop at the number on the card.
Catcher gives a target every pitch and holds the glove still after the catch.
A pitcher who looks tired or whose mechanics are falling apart is done, even if pitches remain on the card.

blocks.title: Game: Target Game and Block Party
blocks.description: Pitchers who still have pitches left on their card throw to a catcher's target: two points if the glove does not move, one point for any strike, zero for a ball, with a strict maximum that ends the game when the card is full. At the same time, catchers in gear play Block Party: the helper tosses eight soft balls into the dirt and the catcher earns a point for every ball kept within arm's reach. Pitchers with no pitches left play Block Party too.
blocks.setup: Pitching plate and catcher in gear with the count card for the target game; a second gear set and soft balls at a throw-down plate for Block Party, well apart from the bullpen lane.
blocks.groups: Scheduled pitchers alternate at the target game; everyone else rotates through Block Party in gear.
coachingPoints: The card ends the game, not the score.
Catchers call out the count with the helper so everyone hears it.
Blocks are scored on keeping the ball in front, not on how it looks.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up and Pitching Log
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. The helper reads each pitcher's total from the card and the coach writes it in the team's pitching log along with the date, so the next eligible day can be found from the league's rest table before the next game. Remind every player to tell a coach or parent about any arm soreness instead of playing through it. Announce the home assignment and the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass, the pitching log and today's count cards on the clipboard.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence so they hear the counts.
coachingPoints: Write the totals today; a count remembered tomorrow is a guess.
The arm-care home assignment is for every player, not only the pitchers.

safety: Count every pitch a player throws, in practice and in games, on a card and in the team pitching log, and follow the league's configured pitch-count and rest table for how many a player may throw and how many days of rest follow; never treat a number you remember as the rule.

Many Little League divisions limit whether a player who has pitched above a certain workload may catch on the same day, and whether a player who has caught a certain number of innings may pitch; the thresholds live in your league's current rulebook and configured table, not in this plan, so check them before every game and practice that involves both roles.
A player who reports arm pain or soreness stops throwing immediately and the parent is informed; coaches do not diagnose, they rest the player and refer to the family.
Catchers wear full gear for every receiving and blocking rep, soft balls are used for blocking, and no player stands behind a hitter or in a throwing lane.
Always check the current Little League rulebook and your league's local rules, because pitch-count and rest requirements change and vary by division and year.
progressions: Add the stretch position for pitchers once the full windup is balanced and repeatable.
Catchers practice throwing footwork to second from the secondary stance with no runner, keeping throw counts modest.
Bullpens with the catcher calling locations, still on the counted plan and still stopping at the card.

items.title: Majors: Live Scrimmage With Situations
items.objective: Players make game decisions under real conditions, with the situation announced before every pitch and points awarded for correct choices by hitters, runners, and fielders rather than for hits and outs.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line thirty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, carioca, side shuffles, walking lunges with a twist, two build-up sprints. Finish with arm circles, arm swings, and trunk rotations while the coach announces the two teams and the first situation of the day.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a line thirty yards out; team lists and a situation list on the coach's clipboard.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave led by a player captain.
coachingPoints: Today's theme: know the situation before every pitch.
Finish together before any ball comes out.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then ninety feet for two minutes and quick-catch at forty-five. Any pitcher scheduled to throw in the scrimmage finishes with the pitching coach and a counted warm-up that is written on the card.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line, moving back on the coach's call, regular baseballs, a count card for any scheduled pitcher.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Front shoulder at the target, elbow up, finish across the body.
Pitchers' warm-up pitches count; the helper writes them down.

blocks.title: Team: Situation Walk-Through
blocks.description: Defense takes the field with no ball. The coach calls a situation and a batted ball, for example 'Runner on second, one out, ground ball to short,' and every player points to where they go and says their job out loud, including backups. Repeat six to eight situations, then run three of them with a fungo and runners in helmets at half speed. Fix the thinking here so the scrimmage can flow.
blocks.setup: Full field with bases, coach at home with a fungo bat and bucket, catcher in gear, runners in helmets at a cone by the dugout.
blocks.groups: Nine on defense, the rest as runners, switching halfway so both teams walk through on defense.
coachingPoints: Everyone has a job on every ball, even if it is backing up a base.
Say it out loud; a quiet defense is a confused defense.
Runners rehearse the reads too: line drive freeze, ground ball go when forced.

blocks.title: Scrimmage Block 1: Runners On
blocks.description: Each half inning starts with runners placed and the count at one ball and one strike to keep the pace up: a runner on first with no outs, then a runner on second with one out, then runners on first and third with one out. The coach pitches from behind an L-screen unless a scheduled pitcher is on a counted plan. Before every pitch the catcher announces the situation and the defense repeats it. Three outs or five batters ends the half inning.
blocks.setup: Full field, L-screen in front of the mound, catcher in gear, helmets on all hitters and runners, a helper tracking outs and the pitch count card if a player pitches.
blocks.groups: Two teams of five to seven switching after each half inning, with positions rotating each inning.
coachingPoints: Catcher calls the situation, defense repeats it, then the pitch.
Runners find the base coach before every pitch.
Coaches freeze the play only when a decision was wrong; let good plays flow.

blocks.title: Scrimmage Block 2: Two Strikes, Bunts, and Tags
blocks.description: Every at-bat starts with two strikes so hitters practice the two-strike approach: choke up a little, widen the base, shorten the swing, and put the ball in play. Every third hitter must bunt with a runner on first, and the coach adds a fungo fly ball with a runner on third at least twice per half inning so tag-ups get practiced. The coach pitches from the L-screen; any player pitching stays on the counted plan.
blocks.setup: Same as Block 1 with a fungo bat beside the coach for the tag-up fly balls.
blocks.groups: Two teams switching after each half inning, positions rotating.
coachingPoints: Two strikes: see it deep, short swing, ball in play; a foul ball is a win.
Runner on third: tag up on any fly ball with fewer than two outs and listen to the third-base coach.
Bunt defense says its play out loud before the pitch.

blocks.title: Game: Situation Scoreboard
blocks.description: The final innings are scored by decisions. Offense: two points for a correct baserunning read, one for a two-strike ball in play, two for a bunt that advances the runner. Defense: two for throwing to the correct base, one for a completed play, one for every backup who was in position. Hits, outs, and runs score nothing, a helper keeps the scoreboard out loud, and the losing team puts away the equipment.
blocks.setup: Same field, a helper with a clipboard announcing points after every play.
blocks.groups: Two teams switching after each half inning until time runs out.
coachingPoints: Announce every point and why, so the whole team learns from every play.
A runner thrown out on a correct, aggressive read still earns the points.
Backups earn points; the quiet jobs matter.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Ask each team to name the best decision the other team made today. Record any pitcher's total in the pitching log. Announce the home assignment and the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected by the players, the pitching log on the clipboard.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Praising the other team's decision is sportsmanship in action.
Write pitch totals before anyone leaves.

safety: The coach pitches from behind an L-screen by default; a player pitches only on a counted plan that follows the league's configured pitch-count and rest table, with every pitch written down.
Helmets on every hitter, on-deck player, and runner; catcher in full gear; one bat in the hitting zone at a time.
Runners avoid collisions and follow your league's current sliding rules; check the rulebook for head-first and must-slide rules before the scrimmage.
Longest throw in the progression is ninety feet, and players who pitched in a game this week stop at sixty.
progressions: Start innings with the game score and inning announced so decisions depend on the score as well as the outs.
Let players call the situation and the defensive alignment without the coach.
Run one full scrimmage game with umpires from the older division to practice talking respectfully with umpires.

items.title: Rainy Day: Indoor Gym Practice
items.objective: Turn a rained-out practice into a real one inside a gym: tennis balls and safety balls only, tee work into a net with no live hitting of hard balls, bases taped on the floor, and every player moving the whole hour.

blocks.title: Gym Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Players spread along one baseline of the basketball court and move to the far baseline and back in waves: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, side shuffles facing both ways, carioca, walking lunges. On the whistle during any movement, everyone freezes in a ready position. Finish with arm circles and arm swings across the body.
blocks.setup: The length of the court with no equipment on the floor. Before players arrive, a coach walks the floor for wet spots and wipes them, and checks that nothing is stored along the walls where players will throw.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, sneakers only, a player captain leading from the front.
coachingPoints: Indoor floors are slick; nobody sprints full speed today.
Ready position freeze on the whistle keeps the drill sharp and reviews the basics.

blocks.title: Wall Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Each player stands at their own cone fifteen feet from the gym wall facing a taped X at chest height and throws a tennis ball at it: wrist flips, then one-knee throws, then standing point-step-throw, catching the rebound each time. After six minutes players pair up along the length of the gym for partner catch with tennis balls at thirty to forty feet, all pairs throwing parallel to the side walls.
blocks.setup: A taped X on the wall every eight feet with a cone fifteen feet out from each; one tennis ball per player; later, pairs lined up down the length of the gym with throws parallel to the walls and never across another pair.
blocks.groups: Every player on their own cone for the wall phase; pairs by arm comfort for partner catch, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Hit the X: accuracy is the only goal at fifteen feet.
Point the glove, step, throw, and catch the rebound with two hands.
Forty feet is the longest throw indoors.

blocks.title: Station 1: Wall Short Hops
blocks.description: Players throw a tennis ball firmly into the wall from twelve feet so it bounces once on the floor and comes back as a short hop, then field it in the triangle: feet wide, glove out front, bare hand on top. They count clean fields out loud and try to get ten in a row. The second half of the station turns the glove over for backhands by throwing to the wall at a slight angle so the ball comes back to the throwing-arm side.
blocks.setup: Taped lines twelve feet from the wall with a cone every eight feet, one tennis ball per player, a bucket of spares.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four to five rotating every 9 minutes on the whistle; every player at their own cone fielding constantly.
coachingPoints: Go get the short hop with the glove moving forward, not back.
Stay low the whole time; the wall never gets tired.
Backhand with the glove-side foot forward and fingers down.

blocks.title: Station 2: Tee Into the Net
blocks.description: One hitter at a time, helmet on, hits safety balls off a tee into a hitting net set against the wall, six swings per turn working inside, middle, and outside tee locations. A painter's-tape square around the tee marks the bat zone and only the hitter is inside it. The other players stand in their own taped boxes fifteen feet away doing shadow swings with no bat, holding a balanced finish for two seconds.
blocks.setup: A hitting net with its back to the wall, a tee on a throw-down plate six feet in front of it, a tape square ten feet around the tee, three or four taped shadow boxes fifteen feet away on the far side, two helmets, a bucket of safety balls.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four to five, 9 minutes per rotation; rotate after every six swings so each player hits twice.
coachingPoints: Safety balls only, and only into the net; nothing hard gets hit indoors.
Bat-zone rule: the tape is a wall while a bat is in the hitter's hands, and the bat goes on the floor before leaving the zone.
Shadow swingers work on balance, not power.

blocks.title: Station 3: Taped-Base Running Footwork
blocks.description: A small diamond of taped bases forty feet apart in half the gym, with a taped finish line fifteen feet past first base. Players run home to first through the finish line at three-quarter speed, then work the banana turn around a cone to first and on toward second, then jog a full lap touching every base. Two runners go at a time, starting on the helper's 'Go!', and nobody slides on the floor.
blocks.setup: Four bases taped on the floor forty feet apart, a taped finish line past first, a cone eight feet outside the baseline for the banana turn, a helper at first base.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four to five, 9 minutes per rotation, two runners at a time with the next pair ready on the plate.
coachingPoints: Through the base to the finish line, not to the base.
Bend early for the turn and touch the inside corner.
Three-quarter speed indoors; sliding is for the grass.

blocks.title: Game: Around the Horn and Hot Box
blocks.description: First six minutes: two teams each stand on a taped diamond and throw a tennis ball around the horn, home to first to second to third and back, earning two points for every catch made without moving the feet and one for a catch with a step; first to twenty wins. Last six minutes: Hot Box, where a runner is caught between two taped bases forty feet apart and two fielders with a tennis ball try to tag the runner with the glove while the runner tries to reach a base; swap runner after each play so everyone runs.
blocks.setup: Two taped diamonds forty feet on a side or the one diamond plus a second set of taped bases, tennis balls, gloves, two coaches awarding points out loud.
blocks.groups: Two teams of four to seven; in Hot Box, groups of four or five with a new runner every play.
coachingPoints: Execution scores, not speed: a clean catch beats a fast throw.
Hot Box tags are soft, with the glove below the shoulders; runners stop before any collision.
Keep throws short and parallel to the walls.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Everyone sits on the center circle. Ask players what the glove does on a short hop and where the tee sits for an outside pitch. Players peel up the tape and collect tennis balls before the home assignment and the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Center court with all equipment collected.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents in the bleachers.
coachingPoints: Leave the gym cleaner than you found it; the custodian decides whether you come back.
The home assignment tonight is a wall and a tennis ball, which every player just practiced.

safety: Tennis balls and safety balls only; no hard baseballs come out of the bag indoors.
No live hitting of hard balls and no front toss indoors; hitting is tee work with safety balls into a net, with a helmet, inside a taped bat zone.
All throws travel parallel to the walls toward a wall or a partner, never across the gym toward another station.
Bases are taped flat on the floor, no sliding, and running is at three-quarter speed; check the floor for wet spots before and during practice.
progressions: Add a second taped X at knee height so wall throws practice a low target.
Short-hop station with a partner throwing instead of the wall, so hops are less predictable.
Around the horn with a transfer requirement: catch, show the ball, then throw.

items.title: One Coach, Twelve Players
items.objective: One adult keeps twelve players busy, safe, and learning for a full hour using the buddy system, two stations that run themselves from laminated cards, and one hitting station the coach never leaves.

blocks.title: Buddy Warm-Up Led by Captains
blocks.description: Players pair up with their buddy for the day as they arrive; buddies stay together all practice. Two captains, rotating every week so everyone gets a turn, lead the dynamic warm-up from a laminated card: jog, skips, high knees, side shuffles, lunges, arm circles. The coach stands where every player is visible and places the station cones while the captains lead.
blocks.setup: A laminated warm-up card with eight movements in large print, cones every ten feet along the foul line and a line twenty yards out, all station equipment in three buckets ready to carry.
blocks.groups: Six pairs in one wave behind the two captains.
coachingPoints: Buddies check each other: if your buddy skips a movement, you both do it again.
The coach never turns his back on the group while setting up.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression in Pairs
blocks.description: Buddies throw across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty, standing throws at thirty, then forty feet with a glove target. The buddy watching the throw says one word of feedback after each throw, 'Step!' if the partner did not step toward the target or 'Good!' if they did, while the coach walks behind one line.
blocks.setup: Six pairs in two facing lines across the foul line, all throws in the same direction, soft baseballs for any nervous catcher.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort; with an odd number the coach becomes a partner.
coachingPoints: One-word feedback only, so buddies coach each other without arguing.
Step toward the glove on every throw.

blocks.title: Station A, Coach-Run: Tee and Front Toss Into the Net
blocks.description: The coach runs this station and does not leave it. One hitter in a helmet inside the bat zone takes five tee swings and five gentle front tosses from the coach kneeling behind a bucket twelve feet away, all into the net. The on-deck buddy does shadow swings at the on-deck cone, and the other pair collects balls behind the net and reloads the bucket. The station sits at the point of a triangle so the coach can see Stations B and C over the hitter's shoulder.
blocks.setup: Hitting net against the backstop, tee, a bat zone of cones fifteen feet around the plate, on-deck cone twenty feet away, bucket of soft baseballs, two helmets. Stations B and C are placed within sixty feet, in the coach's line of sight.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, two buddy pairs each, rotating all three stations every 10 minutes on the coach's phone timer and whistle.
coachingPoints: Helmets on the hitter and on-deck player, one bat in the zone, bat on the ground before leaving.
Watch the ball to the bat; the coach says 'Eyes!' before every toss.
Glance at the other two stations between every hitter.

blocks.title: Station B, Self-Run: Buddy Ground Balls
blocks.description: Buddies stand at two cones twenty feet apart. One rolls ten ground balls, the other fields in the triangle and tosses back, then they swap. A laminated card at the station shows three pictures: feet wide, glove out front, bare hand on top, with the words 'Count your clean fields.' Each pair tries to beat its own count on the second round, and the two pairs at the station report their counts to each other at the whistle.
blocks.setup: Two pairs of cones twenty feet apart on the grass, a bucket of six baseballs per pair, soft baseballs for seven-year-olds, a laminated card on a cone.
blocks.groups: Two buddy pairs per rotation, every player either rolling or fielding at all times.
coachingPoints: Roll slowly and straight at the glove so the buddy succeeds.
Glove out front where the eyes can see the ball into it.
Count out loud; the count keeps buddies honest and busy.

blocks.title: Station C, Self-Run: Bucket Target Throws
blocks.description: A bucket lies on its side thirty feet from a throw-down base, with a cone standing on each side as smaller targets. Buddies take turns throwing five balls each from the base: three points for a ball into the bucket, one point for knocking over a cone, and the buddy retrieves and keeps score on the card's tally box. The card reminds them: point, step, throw.
blocks.setup: Two bucket targets thirty feet from two throw-down bases, aimed at a fence so misses stop, a cone on each side of each bucket, five baseballs per pair, a laminated card with a tally box and a dry-erase marker.
blocks.groups: Two buddy pairs per rotation, one throwing and one retrieving in each pair, swapping every five throws.
coachingPoints: Point the glove at the bucket, step, throw; accuracy wins, not power.
Wait until your buddy is back beside you before the next throw.
Throw toward the fence only.

blocks.title: Game: Tee Scrimmage, Three Outs and Switch
blocks.description: Six players take the field and six bat off the tee at home plate, with the coach standing beside the plate running the tee, the bat zone, and the outs. Batters run the bases live and the defense plays every ball, throwing to the base of the play. Two batting-team buddies serve as base coaches at first and third with the two signals, windmill for go and hands up for stop. Three outs or six batters, then switch sides.
blocks.setup: Full infield with bases, tee on home plate inside the bat zone cones, helmets for every batter and runner, soft baseballs, a bucket beside the coach.
blocks.groups: Two teams of six, buddies on the same team, switching after three outs or six batters.
coachingPoints: The coach stays at home plate where every player and every throw is visible.
Runners look at their buddy base coach before every pitch.
Defense calls the base out loud before the ball is hit.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Buddies sit together on the infield grass and tell each other one thing their buddy did well. Announce next week's captains and the home assignment, then the team cheer. Players carry every bucket and card to the coach's car.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment stacked by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team in buddy pairs, parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Buddy praise builds the team faster than coach praise.
Name next week's captains so they arrive ready to lead.

safety: The coach never leaves the hitting station while a bat is in use; the self-run stations are placed within sixty feet and in direct line of sight.
Helmets on every hitter and on-deck player, one bat in the zone, bat on the ground before leaving the zone, and no bats at the self-run stations.
Self-run stations roll ground balls and throw at targets backed by a fence, so all throws travel away from the other stations.
Soft baseballs for seven- and eight-year-olds and for any player new to catching; the coach checks the buddy pairings so no player is paired with someone far stronger.
progressions: Station B becomes one-hop throws instead of rolls once every pair fields rolled balls cleanly.
Station C moves the bucket to forty feet and adds a one-knee round for accuracy.
A parent volunteer runs the tee scrimmage bases so the coach can hit fungo instead of using the tee.

items.title: Small-Space Practice on a Shared Field
items.objective: Run a full-value practice on half an infield or a strip of foul territory shared with another team, with every throw traveling in one safe direction, no live hitting into shared space, and compact stations that keep everyone moving.

blocks.title: Compact Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: Inside a thirty-by-thirty-foot cone square in your corner of the field, players do movements in place and in short laps around the square: jog laps, skips, high knees, side shuffles along each side, walking lunges across the middle, arm circles and arm swings standing on the corners. Before starting, the coach agrees with the other team's coach on which direction each team will throw.
blocks.setup: Four cones in a thirty-foot square in the space you have been given, with the open side of the square facing the fence you will throw toward.
blocks.groups: Whole team inside the square, a player captain leading.
coachingPoints: Agree on throwing lanes with the other coach before any ball comes out.
Short laps keep everyone moving without leaving your space.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression Along the Line
blocks.description: Pairs line up along the foul line with partners facing each other across it, so every throw travels parallel to the line and toward your own fence, away from the shared team. Wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then back to forty-five for quick-catch. Sixty feet is the limit because space is tight.
blocks.setup: Pairs along the foul line in two facing lines, moving back only along the line, regular baseballs, a coach at each end watching for anyone drifting into the other team's area.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort, odd player with a coach.
coachingPoints: Every throw goes the same direction; if a ball gets away, call 'Ball!' loudly before chasing it.
Front shoulder at the target, step, finish across the body.

blocks.title: Station 1: Short-Hop Triangle
blocks.description: Three players form a triangle fifteen feet on a side with one tennis ball and throw firm one-hoppers to each other, fielding every short hop in the triangle and throwing to the next player. After four minutes the throws go to the glove side and backhand side on purpose so players practice glove angles. A fourth player rotates in every ten fields.
blocks.setup: Triangles of three cones fifteen feet apart on grass or dirt in your corner, one tennis ball per triangle, a bucket of spares.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 9 minutes on the whistle; three in the triangle and one rotating in every ten fields.
coachingPoints: Stay low from start to finish and play the short hop out front.
Firm throws, not hard ones; this is footwork and glove work.
Keep the triangle tight so no throw leaves your space.

blocks.title: Station 2: Tee Into the Net
blocks.description: A hitting net sits with its back to your fence and a tee six feet in front of it. One hitter in a helmet inside the bat zone hits six balls into the net working inside, middle, and outside tee locations, then rotates. The on-deck player shadows at the on-deck cone, and two players reset the tee and collect balls. No front toss today; in shared space, nothing gets hit into the open.
blocks.setup: Net against the fence, tee on a throw-down plate, a bat zone of cones twelve feet around the tee, on-deck cone twenty feet away toward your own space, two helmets, a bucket of baseballs or soft baseballs.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 9 minutes per rotation; rotate after each hitter's six swings.
coachingPoints: Helmets on the hitter and on-deck player, one bat in the zone, bat on the ground before leaving.
Inside pitch out front, outside pitch deeper, same swing.
Hit the net every time; a ball over the net is a ball into someone else's practice.

blocks.title: Station 3: Quick-Hands Transfers
blocks.description: Partners stand twenty feet apart with a tennis ball and play quick-catch: catch with two hands, transfer the ball to the throwing hand in front of the chest while the feet shuffle toward the target, and release in rhythm. Count consecutive catches as a pair, then add a wrinkle: the receiver has to turn to the glove side before throwing, like a relay man. Pairs try to beat their own record.
blocks.setup: Pairs of cones twenty feet apart, parallel to the foul line so throws travel toward your fence, one tennis ball per pair.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 9 minutes per rotation, in pairs the whole time.
coachingPoints: Smooth is fast; a dropped transfer costs more than a slow one.
Feet move first, hands follow.
Turn to the glove side, always.

blocks.title: Team: Four-Corner Throwing
blocks.description: Four cones form a square as large as your space allows, sixty feet on a side if possible, with two or three players at each corner. The ball goes around the square with each receiver catching, turning to the glove side, and throwing to the next corner, then jogging to the back of that corner. After four minutes reverse direction, and for the last three minutes add a second ball so players have to communicate.
blocks.setup: Four cones in the largest square that fits your space, two or three players per corner, two baseballs.
blocks.groups: Whole team spread over the four corners, moving to the next corner after each throw.
coachingPoints: Call the name of the player you are throwing to.
Catch, turn glove side, step, throw: four parts in one rhythm.
With two balls, the loudest corner is the safest corner.

blocks.title: Game: Around the Square Under Control
blocks.description: Same four corners. The team counts clean catches out loud for ninety seconds, where clean means caught without the receiver leaving the cone, and a drop or a chase does not count. Rest, then try to beat the count. Two rounds, team record written down for the next tight-space practice.
blocks.setup: Same four corners, one baseball, a coach with a watch counting aloud.
blocks.groups: Whole team at the corners.
coachingPoints: Execution is the score; a slow, accurate throw counts and a fast, wild one does not.
Breathe between rounds; it is a long day for arms.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee in your square. Ask which way the relay man turns and where the tee sits for an inside pitch. Thank the other team's coach out loud so players see it, announce the home assignment, and finish with the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Cone square with equipment collected by the players.
blocks.groups: Whole team, parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Model courtesy to the team sharing your field.
Remind players the home assignment needs a wall and a tennis ball.

safety: Agree on throwing directions with the other team before practice; every throw today travels toward your own fence and never across shared space.
No front toss or live hitting in shared space; hitting is tee work into a net backed by a fence, with a helmet, inside a cone bat zone.
Tennis balls at the short-hop and transfer stations; throwing distances capped at sixty feet.
Anyone chasing a loose ball calls 'Ball!' first and walks, never runs, into the other team's area.
progressions: Short-hop triangle with baseballs once every player keeps the glove out front on bad hops.
Four-corner throwing with a required transfer and a tag of the cone, like a force play.
Add a fourth station of dry baserunning footwork along the foul line if you have the room.

items.title: Pre-Game Warm-Up Routine
items.objective: Players arrive at first pitch warm, loose, and focused through the same thirty-minute routine every game: a dynamic warm-up, a throwing progression, quick ground balls and fly balls, and a short team talk, usually in foul territory because the infield belongs to the home team or the grounds crew.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up
blocks.description: In foul territory, players move from the foul line to a cone twenty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, side shuffles, carioca, walking lunges, and two build-up runs at three-quarter speed. Finish with arm circles small to large, arm swings across the body, and trunk rotations. A player captain leads so the coaches can check in with the umpires and the other team.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line in your dugout's foul territory and a cone twenty yards out; cleats on, no gloves yet.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave behind the captain.
coachingPoints: Same order every game so players can run it without being told.
Build-up runs are controlled; nobody pulls anything before the game starts.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression
blocks.description: Partners along the foul line, throwing parallel to it: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then out to game distance for the position, with outfielders crow-hopping at ninety feet or so and infielders staying at sixty to seventy, and finish with quick-catch at forty-five. The starting pitcher and catcher leave after the sixty-foot stage to warm up in the bullpen with a coach who writes down every warm-up pitch.
blocks.setup: Pairs along the foul line in two facing lines, moving back along the line, regular baseballs, the bullpen with a coach, a catcher in gear, and the pitch count card.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by position: outfielders together, infielders together, the battery with the pitching coach.
coachingPoints: Game throws only after the whole progression; nobody skips to long throws.
Bullpen warm-up pitches are written down; check your league's current rulebook for what counts toward the game pitch limit.
Finish with quick-catch so hands are ready, not just arms.

blocks.title: Quick Ground Balls
blocks.description: If the infield is available, infielders take their positions and a coach hits three fungo ground balls to each, with throws to first and the first baseman throwing to the catcher. If the infield is not available, the same happens in foul territory with a coach rolling or hitting short ground balls to infielders spread along the line and a player receiving on a throw-down base. Outfielders take ground balls from a helper in the outfield grass and throw to a cutoff cone.
blocks.setup: Fungo bat and bucket for the coach, a throw-down base and a cutoff cone if working in foul territory, catcher in gear if the infield is in use.
blocks.groups: Infielders with the head coach, outfielders with the assistant, the battery still in the bullpen.
coachingPoints: Three clean reps each, not thirty; this is a warm-up, not a lesson.
Chest-high throws to first; good habits start before the first pitch.

blocks.title: Quick Fly Balls
blocks.description: Outfielders take two fly balls each from the assistant coach, one over each shoulder, with a crow-hop throw to a cutoff player at the edge of the grass. Infielders take two pop-ups each from the head coach, calling the ball three times, while the catcher, if finished in the bullpen, takes two pop-ups in gear. Everything is thrown rather than hit if space is shared or tight.
blocks.setup: Assistant coach with a bucket in the outfield, head coach with a bucket in foul territory, cutoff cone at the infield edge.
blocks.groups: Outfielders with the assistant, infielders with the head coach.
coachingPoints: Call it three times, catch it above the eyes with two hands.
Hit the cutoff man; nobody shows off an arm before the game.

blocks.title: Team Talk
blocks.description: Team gathers in front of the dugout, gloves off, helmets for the first three hitters within reach. The coach reads the lineup and positions, names one defensive focus for the day, such as hitting the cutoff man, and gives the sportsmanship reminder: respect the umpire's calls, cheer teammates, and shake hands at the end whatever the score. The captains lead the cheer and the team takes the field together.
blocks.setup: In front of the dugout, lineup card ready, the pitch count card handed to the person who will keep the count during the game.
blocks.groups: Whole team, coaches in the middle.
coachingPoints: One focus, not five; players remember one.
The sportsmanship reminder happens every game, win or lose, so it becomes who the team is.
Make sure the pitch counter and the lineup card are in the right hands before the first pitch.

safety: The routine runs in foul territory unless the umpire or the other coach confirms the infield is yours; throws travel parallel to the foul line, away from spectators and the other team.
Starting pitcher's bullpen pitches are counted and written down; the game pitch count and rest rules come from your league's configured pitch-count and rest table and the current rulebook.
Catchers wear full gear for every bullpen and every pop-up; helmets on the first hitters before the team takes the field.
Fly balls are thrown, not hit, whenever space is shared or players are still warming up.
progressions: Let the captains run the whole routine while the coaches handle lineup cards and umpire meetings.
Add a two-minute situation quiz to the team talk: 'Runner on first, one out, ground ball to short, where does it go?'
Build an on-deck routine for hitters that matches the mental preparation lesson.

items.title: Intermediate and Juniors: Leads, Steals, and Pickoffs
items.objective: Runners take safe primary and secondary leads, read the pitcher's first move, and get back on pickoffs; pitchers learn simple, legal pickoff footwork on a counted plan; catchers and middle infielders defend the steal. This plan applies only in divisions whose rules allow runners to lead off before the pitch; check your league's current Little League rulebook before using it.

blocks.title: Dynamic Warm-Up With Lead-Off Shuffles
blocks.description: Foul line to a cone line thirty yards out and back: jog, skips, high knees, butt kicks, carioca, side shuffles, walking lunges, two build-up sprints. Then lead-off footwork on the grass: everyone faces the coach in a spread grid, shuffles two steps right on 'Lead!', shuffles two more on 'Secondary!', and on 'Back!' crosses over and sprints two steps left, or on 'Go!' crosses over and sprints two steps right. Finish with arm circles and arm swings.
blocks.setup: Cones every ten feet along the foul line and a line thirty yards out, then a grid of one cone per player in the outfield facing the coach.
blocks.groups: Whole team in one wave, then everyone on their own cone for the shuffle calls.
coachingPoints: Shuffle steps stay low with the weight balanced so either direction is possible.
The crossover step is the first step both back to the base and toward the next one.

blocks.title: Throwing Progression and Dry Pickoff Footwork
blocks.description: Partners across the foul line: wrist flips at fifteen feet, one-knee throws at twenty-five, rocker-step throws at forty, regular throws at sixty, then one hundred feet for three minutes, then quick-catch at forty-five. Pitchers scheduled to work today finish with dry footwork with the pitching coach, no ball: from the stretch, the step-off, the jump turn to first for right-handers, and the step toward first for left-handers, five repetitions each.
blocks.setup: Partners facing across the foul line, regular baseballs; a throw-down rubber on flat ground with a cone where first base would be for the dry footwork.
blocks.groups: Pairs matched by arm comfort, then scheduled pitchers with the pitching coach while everyone else does quick-catch.
coachingPoints: One hundred feet is the longest throw today.
Dry footwork first; the arm has not earned pickoff throws yet.
Stepping off the rubber before throwing to a base is the simplest legal move and the one to learn first.

blocks.title: Team: Rules Check and Lead-Off Basics
blocks.description: Everyone gathers at first base. The coach explains that in this division runners may lead off before the pitch, that in many younger divisions runners must stay on the base until the pitch reaches the batter, and that the exact rules, including balk rules, come from the league's current rulebook, which the coach has read this week. Then the basics: a primary lead is a few shuffle steps the runner can get back from in one crossover step and a dive, starting conservative; a secondary lead is two more shuffles as the pitch is delivered; on any pickoff the first move is the crossover step back to the bag. Players walk it, then jog it, with a coach on the mound in the stretch.
blocks.setup: Full infield with bases, a coach on the mound holding a ball in the stretch, a cone marking a conservative primary lead and a second cone marking the secondary lead.
blocks.groups: Whole team taking turns at first base in groups of three, with everyone else watching from foul territory for this one segment only.
coachingPoints: Start with a lead you can get back from easily; distance grows with confidence over weeks, not minutes.
Eyes on the pitcher, not on the base; the base does not move.
The dive back to first happens only after it has been taught on grass and only where your league permits head-first returns; until then, get back standing.

blocks.title: Station 1: Leads and Jumps
blocks.description: A coach or an older player stands on a throw-down rubber in the outfield grass in the stretch position with a ball, and runners take turns at a throw-down first base forty feet away. Against a right-handed pitcher the runner goes when the front heel lifts toward home and gets back when the back foot steps off the rubber or the shoulder turns toward first; against a left-hander the runner waits longer and reads the back knee and the step. Each runner takes six reads, mixing pitches and pickoff fakes with no throw. Four players rotate as runner, fake pitcher, and two observers who call out 'Go!' or 'Back!' as the move happens.
blocks.setup: Throw-down rubber and first base forty feet apart in the outfield grass, a second base cone sixty feet away for the runner to break toward, one ball for the fake pitcher.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four rotating every 12 minutes on the whistle; roles change after every six reads.
coachingPoints: Read the heel and the shoulder, not the hands.
A good jump beats a big lead every time.
Observers call it out loud so the reading becomes a shared language.

blocks.title: Station 2: Pitcher Pickoff Footwork
blocks.description: Pitchers work from a throw-down rubber on flat ground with a player at a base forty feet away. Right-handers learn the step-off and throw, then the jump turn to first; left-handers learn to lift the knee and step directly toward first before throwing; everyone learns the inside move to second, a slow turn toward second during the leg lift. Each pitcher throws no more than eight pickoff throws at this station, with the rest done dry, because pickoffs are throws and the arm is counting them.
blocks.setup: Two throw-down rubbers on flat grass each with a base forty feet away and a receiver with a glove, a cone marking second base for the inside move, the pitching coach with a count card.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation: two pitchers working, two receivers, swapping halfway. Non-pitchers learn the footwork dry and act as receivers.
coachingPoints: Step off the rubber first when in doubt; it is the simplest legal move in every rulebook.
Pickoff throws go to the inside of the base at knee height so the tag is quick.
Eight throws maximum per pitcher, written down; check your league's balk rules for your division before using any move in a game.

blocks.title: Station 3: Steal Defense
blocks.description: A catcher in full gear sets up in the secondary stance with a coach lobbing pitches from twenty feet; on 'Runner!' the catcher receives, transfers with the ball in front of the chest, steps toward second with the throwing-side foot replacing the glove-side foot, and throws to the shortstop or second baseman straddling the bag. The fielder catches, drops the glove to the front of the base, and lets an imaginary runner slide into it. Runners at this station jog toward second and peel off without sliding. Catchers throw no more than ten times each.
blocks.setup: Home plate and second base with a coach lobbing from twenty feet in front of the plate, catcher's gear, two middle infielders alternating at the bag, a runner's cone near first.
blocks.groups: Three groups of four, 12 minutes per rotation: catcher, two middle infielders, runner, rotating every five throws.
coachingPoints: Transfer in front of the chest; the feet make the throw quick, not the arm.
Fielder straddles the bag, catches, and drops the glove to the front edge; the runner slides into the tag.
Ten throws per catcher, counted; quality beats quantity.

blocks.title: Game: The Steal Game
blocks.description: Runners at first against a full battery and middle infield. A coach on the mound pitches from the stretch at a shortened distance with a real leg lift so runners get live reads, or a scheduled pitcher throws counted pitches. Runners earn two points for a good jump on the heel lift and one for getting back standing on a pickoff; the catcher earns two for a throw on the bag side at knee height, the fielder one for the correct tag position, and the pitcher one for a legal pickoff that holds the runner close. Safe or out does not decide points, and everyone runs and everyone fields.
blocks.setup: Full infield with bases, catcher in full gear, coach or counted pitcher on the mound, helmets on all runners, a helper keeping score aloud and counting every throw by the catcher and pitcher.
blocks.groups: Two teams switching after every five runners, positions rotating within the defense.
coachingPoints: Announce every point and why: the jump, the throw, the tag.
Runners slide feet first with hands up or peel off; no head-first slides into second today.
Catcher and pitcher throw counts are written down; the card ends their part of the game.

blocks.title: Wrap-Up
blocks.description: Take a knee behind the mound. Ask what the runner reads on a right-hander and what the simplest legal pickoff is. Repeat that leads and steals apply only where the division's rules allow them and that the current rulebook decides. Record pitcher and catcher throw totals, announce the home assignment, and finish with the team cheer.
blocks.setup: Infield grass with equipment collected by the players, the count cards on the clipboard.
blocks.groups: Whole team with parents at the fence.
coachingPoints: Players answer; coaches confirm.
Write the throw totals before anyone leaves.

safety: Leads, steals, and pickoffs are practiced only for divisions whose rules allow runners to lead off before the pitch; check your league's current Little League rulebook and local rules before running this plan.

Pickoff throws and steal throws are throws: pitchers are capped at eight pickoff throws at the station, catchers at ten steal throws, everything is written on the count card, and any scheduled pitcher follows the league's configured pitch-count and rest table.
Runners wear helmets, slide feet first with hands up or peel off, and never slide head first into second; dives back to first are taught separately on grass and only where the league permits them.
Tags are made with the glove at the front of the base; fielders never block the base with a leg or body.
progressions: Add the delayed steal and the first-and-third situation once primary leads are safe and consistent.
Left-handed pitchers work their move to first with a live runner reading the knee.
Catchers throw to third on a steal attempt with the third baseman learning the tag.
